attractions.name: Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway

scary.notes: The only genuine fright risk is the tornado sequence, where the room spins, the lights strobe and the soundtrack goes loud and chaotic for about forty seconds. Toddlers who dislike sudden noise sometimes cry there and are fine by the next scene. There are no drops, no restraints beyond a lap bar, and the vehicles never leave a walking pace. Kids who handle the Haunted Mansion at Magic Kingdom will be untroubled here.

accessibility.notes: One car per train is built to load a wheelchair or ECV directly, so you can stay seated the whole way. Ask at the entrance and a cast member will route you through the accessible queue. The pre-show cartoon runs with open captions on the screen.

attractions.summary: A trackless dark ride behind the Chinese Theatre screen that turns a Mickey cartoon into eight rooms of gags, with no height requirement.
description: This is the ride that replaced The Great Movie Ride inside the Chinese Theatre in 2020, and it is the single best attraction in the park for a family that includes somebody under 38 inches. The premise is simple: you walk into a movie theater to watch a new Mickey Mouse cartoon, the screen turns out to be a doorway, and you spend five minutes inside the cartoon aboard a runaway train car driven by Goofy.

Mechanically it is a trackless ride system, the same family of technology as Rise of the Resistance. Cars move independently, swivel, back up, and split into separate paths, which means two vehicles in the same room are often watching different gags at the same moment. Disney uses that to hide the seams: the ride is a series of eight-ish set pieces, and no two ride-throughs give you the same viewing angles.

The art direction leans hard into the modern Paul Rudish cartoon shorts rather than classic 1930s Mickey, so the color is loud and the gags are fast. If you have only seen Mickey on merchandise, the tone will surprise you. It is genuinely funny in a slapstick way, and the earworm song running underneath it will be stuck in your head until dinner.
experience: The queue is worth walking slowly. It runs through a lobby of fake movie posters for cartoon shorts that do not exist, and the jokes in the small print are better than most of the ride. If the standby line is short you will be pushed through this in ninety seconds, which is a shame. The pre-show is a genuine animated short, about three minutes, shown standing up in a small theater.

Once you board, the beats go roughly: a runaway train sequence, a tumble into a factory, a carnival, a rainstorm and waterfall room where you will catch a light mist, then the tornado, then a dance-hall finale. The waterfall room is the prettiest thing in the ride and the easiest to miss because most people are looking at the wrong wall. Look up and left as you pass under the falls.

Seat choice matters less than on a tracked ride, but the front row of each car has the clearest sightline to the projected screens, and the back row catches more of the physical sets. If you are riding with a nervous kid, ask for the back of the second car, which spends the tornado scene further from the strobes.
tips: The queue splits into two lines just past the poster lobby. Neither is faster, but the right-hand side loads the cars with the better view of the waterfall room.
This ride absorbs an enormous number of people per hour, so a posted 45-minute wait usually resolves in about 30. Do not burn a Lightning Lane Multi Pass here unless the board says 60 or more.
It is one of the very few attractions at this park with no height requirement, which makes it the natural rider-switch-free option while your group splits for Tower of Terror.
Waits collapse in the last hour of the night because everyone is at Fantasmic or heading to the exit. Riding at close is the single easiest win in the park.
There is no on-ride photo, so you can hold a toddler on your lap for the whole ride without worrying about a camera catching a bad moment.
attractions.bestTime: First 45 minutes of the day, or the last hour before close when Fantasmic pulls the crowd away.
attractions.typicalWait: Usually 30 to 60 minutes midday; drops under 25 at rope drop and in the final hour.

faqs.q: Is there a height requirement for Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway?
faqs.a: No. Any guest who can sit up unassisted with an adult can ride, including infants. It is the flagship attraction at Hollywood Studios that the whole family can do together, which matters in a park where seven other rides have height sticks.

faqs.q: Is Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway scary for toddlers?
faqs.a: Mostly no. The tornado scene is loud, spins the room and uses strobe-like lighting for roughly forty seconds, and that is the part that upsets sensitive preschoolers. There are no drops and the vehicles stay at a walking pace throughout.

faqs.q: Do you get wet on Runaway Railway?
faqs.a: Only a fine mist in the waterfall room, and only for a few seconds. Nobody needs a poncho. Phones and cameras are fine out in the open.

faqs.q: How long is the ride?
faqs.a: About five minutes of ride time, plus a three-minute standing pre-show and a queue you should walk slowly. Budget twelve minutes from the moment you tap in even if there is no line.

faqs.q: Is it worth a Lightning Lane Multi Pass selection?
faqs.a: Rarely. Capacity is high and the posted wait is usually inflated by ten to fifteen minutes. Spend your Multi Pass on Slinky Dog Dash or Tower of Terror and ride this at night.

attractions.name: Citizens of Hollywood

scary.notes: Nothing here frightens anyone. The only discomfort is social: the performers pull guests into bits, and shy adults get chosen more often than they would like. If you do not want to be part of a scene, stand at the back of the semicircle rather than the front.

accessibility.notes: Fully step-free street performance with no seating, so wheelchair and ECV users can park anywhere in the crowd. Sightlines are best from the curb on the Sunset Boulevard side. There is no amplification for some of the smaller bits, which makes them hard to follow with hearing loss.

attractions.summary: Roaming improv performers playing 1940s Hollywood hopefuls, doing short street scenes up and down Hollywood Boulevard through the day.
description: A troupe of improvisers works Hollywood Boulevard in character as a fixed cast of Hollywood types: a public works crew, a starlet, a talent agent, a director, a security officer. They perform short scenes on the street, mostly unannounced, and they are the reason the front of this park has a personality that the entrance plazas of the other three Florida parks do not.

The material is genuinely improvised and genuinely funny, and the performers are skilled enough to make a bit out of whatever a guest says back to them. Long-timers plan around specific scheduled sets, particularly the group numbers that happen on the small stage near the intersection with Sunset Boulevard. Everyone else stumbles into them, watches four minutes, and moves on.
This is a low-commitment, high-return use of ten minutes. It also plays completely differently for adults and for kids: the wordplay lands for grown-ups, and the physical comedy carries the children.
tips: The scheduled group sets are listed in the app under entertainment, not under attractions. Most people never look there and never see them.
The performers are in character before and after the set. If you talk to the talent agent on the sidewalk you will get a two-minute private scene for free.
Best shade is under the awnings on the east side of the boulevard, which is also where the performers tend to stage the smaller bits.
Repeat visitors: the cast rotates material by day of week, so a set you saw on Tuesday will not be the set you see on Saturday.
attractions.bestTime: Late morning and again in the two hours before the nighttime show, when the boulevard is busiest.
attractions.typicalWait: No wait. Scenes run roughly every 30 to 45 minutes at various points along the street.

attractions.name: Wonderful World of Animation

scary.notes: Projection only, with fireworks-style bursts and some loud musical stings. A few villain segments go dark and loud for fifteen seconds at a time. Small children who are already tired at the end of a long day sometimes find the volume more than the visuals unpleasant.

accessibility.notes: Standing-only viewing on flat pavement in front of the Chinese Theatre, with designated accessible viewing marked by cast members roughly twenty minutes ahead. Sightlines are entirely about height of the people in front of you, so a wheelchair user should claim the marked area early.

attractions.summary: A projection show on the Chinese Theatre facade that runs through nearly a century of Disney animation in about twelve minutes.
description: The facade of the Chinese Theatre is used as a projection surface for a rapid tour through Disney and Pixar animation, structured loosely around the idea that a single pencil line becomes everything that followed. It is a mapping show rather than a fireworks show, which means the building itself appears to fold, melt, and rebuild.

It is short, it is free, it requires no reservation and no viewing spot claimed hours in advance, and it plays after park close on many nights. Compared with Fantasmic it demands almost nothing from you. Compared with Fantasmic it also gives you less: there is no cast, no water, no live element, just a very well-produced projection reel.

The best argument for it is the crowd flow. Because it plays on the boulevard where everyone is already walking out, you can watch it while you leave. That makes it one of the highest-value twelve minutes in the park for a family that skipped the amphitheater.
tips: Stand between the flagpole and the hat-shaped planter for the flattest, least distorted angle on the projection. Straight-on beats close-up here.
If a shorter projection reel plays first, that is a separate piece and not the main show. Do not walk off during the gap.
The whole boulevard is standing room, so put small children on shoulders or stand further back where the crowd thins and the sightline is actually better.
Repeat visitors: on nights when the show runs twice, the second showing plays to perhaps a fifth of the crowd and you can stand dead center.
attractions.bestTime: The final showing of the night, when most of the crowd has already left through the turnstiles.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue. Arrive 10 to 15 minutes early for a center position on the boulevard.

attractions.name: Disney Movie Magic

scary.notes: Clips from live-action Disney films, including a few action sequences with gunfire sound effects and explosions. Nothing graphic, but the audio is punchy and a couple of the pirate and superhero segments startle toddlers. Adults find it nostalgic rather than tense.

accessibility.notes: Same standing viewing area and same accessible viewing zone as the animation projection show that follows it. Flat pavement throughout, no steps.

attractions.summary: A ten-minute projection reel of live-action Disney films on the Chinese Theatre, usually programmed just before the animation show.
description: This is the live-action companion piece to the animation projection show, cut from Disney's non-animated catalog: adventure films, superhero films, pirate films, the occasional musical. It leans on big orchestral moments and works best if you have actually seen the movies, which makes it a much better watch for adults than for children.

It usually plays as the opening act on the same nights as the animation show, and because it starts earlier, most of the crowd is still walking around and paying no attention. That is exactly why it is worth catching. Ten minutes of good projection work with room to breathe beats the same ten minutes shoulder to shoulder.
Projection lineups on this facade are rotated by Disney from time to time, so treat the running order as flexible and check the entertainment tab in the app on the day.
tips: Because it starts before the crowd assembles, you can walk up two minutes before showtime and still stand center.
The projection is brightest and sharpest on the upper tiers of the theater facade. Stand far enough back to keep the whole building in frame.
Skip it entirely if you are trying to make Fantasmic. The two are scheduled tightly and the amphitheater fills faster than this street does.
Repeat visitors: the clip selection has been revised more than once since 2017, so a segment you remember may no longer be in the reel.
attractions.bestTime: Right at its posted start time; the boulevard is still moving and you can stand anywhere.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue. Walk-up viewing.

attractions.name: Disney Skyliner

scary.notes: Gondolas hang roughly sixty feet up and sway slightly at the towers. People with a fear of heights or of enclosed spaces genuinely do not enjoy this, and the cabins do not open. Everyone else finds it calm to the point of sleepy.

accessibility.notes: Standard cabins load from a moving platform; ask for an accessible cabin and the line will be slowed or stopped for boarding, which takes a few extra minutes. Cabins are not air conditioned but have passive vents, and they get hot when the system pauses.

attractions.summary: The gondola line from just outside the park gate to EPCOT and four resort hotels, and the fastest way out at closing time.
description: The Skyliner station sits immediately outside the Hollywood Studios turnstiles, and the line from here splits at Caribbean Beach toward EPCOT's International Gateway, Riviera Resort, Pop Century and Art of Animation. It is free, it runs continuously while the parks are open, and it beats a bus in almost every direction it serves.

Treat it as an attraction, not just as transport. The stretch over the water between Hollywood Studios and Caribbean Beach at dusk is one of the better views on Disney property, and it costs you nothing. It is also the only place in a Disney park where you get fifteen quiet, seated, non-queueing minutes with your own family.

The obvious catch is weather. Lightning within range stops the system, and when it stops it can strand a very large number of people at once. The recovery line at the Hollywood Studios station after an evening storm is one of the worst waits on property.
tips: Going to EPCOT you must change at Caribbean Beach. It is a walk across the platform, not a new queue, and it adds about four minutes.
If the sky looks bad and you need to be somewhere, take the bus. Skyliner shutdowns cascade and the queue after one can run past an hour.
Cabins have no fans and no air conditioning; the vents only work while moving. Do not board with an infant right after a stoppage.
Repeat visitors: request a cabin to yourself by asking at the load platform. Cast members will usually accommodate it outside peak departure, which turns the ride into a genuine break.
attractions.bestTime: About 45 minutes before sunset for the best light over Hourglass Lake.
attractions.typicalWait: Walk-on most of the day; 20 to 40 minutes in the surge right after park close.

attractions.name: Friendship Boats to EPCOT and the BoardWalk

scary.notes: A slow covered launch on a flat canal. There is nothing here to frighten anyone at any age. The only real hazard is boarding in a swell after a storm, when the dock moves under you.

accessibility.notes: Boats board over a short ramp and have designated wheelchair spaces; crew members will hold the boat while you position. Larger ECVs occasionally have to wait for a specific boat, so allow extra time.

attractions.summary: The slow canal launch linking the park to the BoardWalk, Yacht and Beach Club, Swan and Dolphin, and EPCOT's back gate.
description: A small fleet of covered boats runs the canal between the Hollywood Studios dock, the Epcot resort hotels and the International Gateway at EPCOT. The full run to EPCOT takes about twenty minutes with all the stops, which is slower than the Skyliner but far more pleasant than standing in a bus queue.

For anyone staying at the BoardWalk, Yacht Club, Beach Club, Swan, Dolphin or Swan Reserve, this is the sensible way home at night: you walk out of the park, turn left, and you are usually aboard within ten minutes. Boats keep running for about an hour after close.
The boats also do something the buses do not, which is let you sit down while the crowd surge dissipates. If your feet are done at 8pm, the boat is a better decision than the walk.
tips: Sit on the left side heading toward EPCOT for the better view of the BoardWalk waterfront and, on many nights, the tail end of the EPCOT fireworks over the trees.
Boats stop for lightning just like the Skyliner but recover faster, because the docks are sheltered.
The walk from the dock to the BoardWalk or Yacht Club is roughly twenty minutes on foot, so on a short queue the boat is genuinely faster, not just easier.
Repeat visitors: at close, the boat queue is almost always shorter than the bus queue for these five hotels, and it starts loading before the buses stage.
attractions.bestTime: Right at park close, when the bus stops are three deep and the dock is not.
attractions.typicalWait: Five to fifteen minutes most of the day; up to 30 in the first surge after the nighttime show.

attractions.name: Mickey & Minnie Starring in Red Carpet Dreams

scary.notes: An indoor, quiet, well-lit meet with a cast member managing the pace. Children who are wary of costumed characters do better here than at outdoor meets because the room is calm and the queue is short.

accessibility.notes: Step-free indoor queue and meeting rooms with room to turn a wheelchair. Characters come to you rather than the other way around, and cast members will adjust the greeting for a guest who cannot stand for the photo.

attractions.summary: Two separate air-conditioned rooms just off Commissary Lane where you meet Mickey Mouse in one and Minnie Mouse in the other.
description: Tucked down the short side street between Echo Lake and the Chinese Theatre, this is a two-room character meet: Mickey Mouse in a sorcerer setting on one side, Minnie Mouse in a movie-star setting on the other. You queue once and see both, and PhotoPass photographers are in each room.

What makes it useful is the air conditioning and the pace. Most character meets at Walt Disney World put you in a hot outdoor line for a rushed thirty seconds. This one is indoors, the queue moves at a reasonable clip, and cast members do not rush families with young children.
It also fills a real gap in this park. Hollywood Studios has fewer character meets than Magic Kingdom, and this is the one that a first-time family with small children should not skip.
tips: The queue is one line for two rooms, so the posted wait covers both greetings. A 25-minute post is really 25 minutes for two characters.
Late afternoon is quietest here because everybody is queueing for rides or heading toward Sunset Boulevard.
Bring anything you want signed. Both characters sign, and the room is calm enough that autographs do not hold up the line.
Repeat visitors: this is one of the few indoor sit-and-cool-down-adjacent spots in the middle of the park, and the queue itself is an air-conditioned twenty minutes on a brutal afternoon.
attractions.bestTime: Between 3pm and 5pm, when the ride queues peak and the character lines empty out.
attractions.typicalWait: 15 to 35 minutes for both rooms; longest just after park opening.

attractions.name: The Great Movie Ride
attractions.closedNote: Closed August 13, 2017. The Chinese Theatre show building was gutted and reopened in March 2020 as Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway.

scary.notes: The gangster and western scenes involved live performers, gunfire effects and a hijacking of the tram, and the Alien sequence was genuinely frightening for children. It is listed here for reference only; the attraction no longer operates.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The attraction is not operating and the show building now houses Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway.

attractions.summary: The park's original anchor attraction, a 22-minute tram tour through recreated movie scenes; closed in 2017 and replaced by Runaway Railway.
description: For twenty-eight years this was the reason the Chinese Theatre existed. A slow tram carried you through full-size recreations of scenes from Hollywood history, with live cast members who hijacked the vehicle partway through and stayed in character for the rest of the trip. It was long, it was strange, and nothing else at Walt Disney World was like it.

It closed in August 2017 and the building was rebuilt for Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway, which opened in March 2020. People still search for it by name, and cast members still get asked about it daily, which is why it belongs on any honest list of this park's attractions.
If you want to see what remains, the exterior of the Chinese Theatre and the forecourt handprints are unchanged, and a few of the old attraction's design ideas survive in the shape of the new queue.
tips: Do not plan around this attraction. It is gone and the show building is fully rebuilt.
The forecourt cement handprints and footprints in front of the theater are original to the park's opening and are still worth two minutes.
If you are chasing the same feeling, the closest thing operating at Walt Disney World today is the Haunted Mansion at Magic Kingdom for pacing and Runaway Railway for the scene-hopping structure.
Repeat visitors: the ride's old load area is roughly where the Runaway Railway pre-show theater now sits, which is why that room feels so much larger than it needs to be.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.

attractions.name: Star Wars: A Galaxy Far, Far Away
attractions.closedNote: The Center Stage show in front of the Chinese Theatre stopped performing in 2020 and has not returned; Star Wars character appearances moved to Galaxy's Edge and Star Wars Launch Bay.

scary.notes: A daytime stage show with villains appearing at high volume. Historical entry only; it no longer performs.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The show does not currently perform, and the Center Stage area in front of the Chinese Theatre is used for other purposes.

attractions.summary: A short daytime stage show of Star Wars characters and film clips on Hollywood Boulevard; it has not performed since 2020.
description: This was a compact stage show in front of the Chinese Theatre that brought out characters from across the Star Wars films with clip montages between appearances. It ran several times a day and was the easiest way to see a large number of Star Wars characters in one place before Galaxy's Edge opened.

It stopped performing in 2020 and has not been reinstated. Star Wars character encounters at this park now happen inside Galaxy's Edge, where they are roaming and unscheduled, and at Star Wars Launch Bay in Animation Courtyard, where they are a queued meet.
It is listed here because people still look for it by name when planning a Star Wars day at Hollywood Studios and deserve a straight answer.
tips: For Star Wars characters today, walk Galaxy's Edge in the first two hours after opening; the roaming encounters are most frequent then.
Star Wars Launch Bay in Animation Courtyard is the reliable, queued alternative and is rarely busy.
Do not confuse this with the nighttime Star Wars fireworks show, which is also not in the current lineup.
Repeat visitors: the Center Stage platform in front of the theater is still there and is used for other programming, so an empty stage does not mean this show is coming back.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.

attractions.name: Star Tours: The Adventures Continue

scary.notes: Nothing here is frightening in a horror sense, but the cabin pitches hard and the 3D screen fills your whole field of view, which is exactly the combination that makes people queasy. Villain segments are loud and confrontational, and the opening sequence includes a sudden hard drop of the cabin. Children who are fine on roller coasters sometimes hate this one and vice versa.

accessibility.notes: You must transfer from a wheelchair or ECV into a standard simulator seat with a lap belt; the cabin floor is level with the load platform. A non-motion viewing option is not offered, so if the motion is the problem the answer is to skip it. Reflective 3D glasses fit over most prescription frames.

attractions.summary: A randomized 3D flight simulator through the Star Wars galaxy, with dozens of possible scene combinations so no two flights match.
description: Star Tours opened at this park in December 1989 as a straight simulator ride with one fixed film. In 2011 it was rebuilt from the ground up in 3D with a randomized structure, and that is the version you ride today. The ride computer assembles each flight from a pool of opening scenes, planet destinations, hologram messages and finales, which produces a very large number of possible combinations.

That randomization is the whole reason people ride it repeatedly. Regulars chase specific segments the way people chase songs at a concert, and the variety is why an attraction from 1989 still holds a real line in 2026. Disney has added new destinations over the years as new films arrived, so the pool keeps growing.

Mechanically it is a forty-passenger cabin on a motion base with a wraparound 3D screen, which means the motion is short-throw and sharp rather than sweeping. It is a genuinely rough ride for anyone prone to motion sickness, and considerably worse than Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run on that front.
experience: The queue is one of the better ones at this park and the reason to go standby rather than Lightning Lane at least once. A full-size droid works a luggage scanner, another runs the departures desk, and the announcements over the terminal PA are worth listening to. The pre-show room does a security screening bit that pays off later in the ride.

In the cabin, everyone is a passenger; there is no interactivity. The flight is roughly a bad takeoff, a hologram transmission, one planet sequence, a second transmission, a second planet sequence and a landing, cut together to about five minutes. The cabin lurches forward and back on impacts, and the seat harnesses stay loose, so you feel more movement than the machine is actually producing.

Sit in the middle rows if you can. The front row puts you close enough to the screen that the 3D separates badly at the edges, and the back rows amplify the pitch. Middle of the middle is the smoothest seat and the best-registered 3D image.
tips: The 40-inch requirement is measured strictly with shoes on. Borderline children get an all-day wristband at the first measurement so they are not re-measured at every ride.

Ask a cast member at the load door for a specific starting planet and they cannot help you, but the ride does bias toward newer destinations at busier times of day. Riding twice in a row almost always produces two different flights.
This is the single most reliable nausea trigger at the park. If you are the kind of person who cannot read in a car, ride it before you eat, not after.
3D glasses are recycled bins near the exit, and there is a stack of larger frames on request for anyone wearing glasses already.

Repeat visitors: the pre-show scanner bit selects a rebel spy from the group standing in front of you, and standing directly beneath the scanner meaningfully raises your odds of being the one on screen.
attractions.bestTime: First hour after opening, or during the nighttime show when the Echo Lake side of the park empties.
attractions.typicalWait: 20 to 45 minutes for most of the day; walk-on levels late.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Star Tours?
faqs.a: 40 inches. It is measured with shoes on and hats off at the entrance, and a borderline guest who clears will be given a colored wristband so they do not get re-measured at other attractions that day.

faqs.q: Is Star Tours the same ride every time?
faqs.a: No. The film is assembled from a pool of opening scenes, planets, hologram messages and finales, so two consecutive rides will almost certainly differ. That is the main argument for riding it more than once.

faqs.q: Does Star Tours make people sick?
faqs.a: More than any other ride at this park. The combination of a hard-throw motion base and a full-field 3D screen affects a lot of people who have no trouble on coasters. Sit in a middle row, keep your eyes on the center of the screen, and do not ride straight after a heavy meal.

faqs.q: Is Star Tours scary for young children?
faqs.a: Not in a horror sense, but it is loud, dark and physically jolty, and villain characters confront the cabin directly. Children right at the 40-inch line often find it more intense than they expected. Runaway Railway is the gentler alternative in the same park.

faqs.q: Is there a single rider line?
faqs.a: No. Star Tours does not offer single rider. It does offer rider switch, so one adult can wait with a child under 40 inches and then ride without re-queueing.

attractions.name: Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular!

scary.notes: The pyrotechnics are the issue, not the content. Several explosions are big enough to be felt in the chest from the middle of the amphitheater, and gunfire effects are loud and repeated. Toddlers who are fine with fireworks are usually fine here; toddlers who flinch at fireworks will not last past the truck fight.

accessibility.notes: Accessible seating is on the flat lower rows, entered from the left side of the amphitheater, and there is no step-up required. Sign language interpretation is offered on a published schedule rather than at every performance. The bench seating has no backs, which matters for a 30-minute show.

attractions.summary: A 30-minute live stunt show in a covered amphitheater that stages and then explains big-budget action sequences, running since the park opened in 1989.
description: This has been running since the park's opening year and the concept has never needed changing: performers stage a series of action sequences as though a film crew were shooting them, then a director character stops and explains how each effect was achieved. It works because it takes the audience seriously. The show is genuinely teaching you about squibs, breakaway props, fire gels and fall pads while entertaining you.

The set is enormous. The famous opening recreates a temple raid complete with a rolling boulder, then breaks down into flats and rotates away to reveal a Cairo marketplace built on the same footprint. The final act adds a truck, a plane, and a large amount of fire.

It is one of only two big live-performer shows left at this park with a real production budget behind it. Whatever else you cut from a Hollywood Studios day, this is not the thing to cut if you have somebody in the group who likes films.
experience: Doors open about twenty minutes before showtime and the amphitheater seats roughly two thousand, which means arriving fifteen minutes early is almost always enough. Before the show starts, a casting director works the crowd picking volunteer extras for the marketplace scene. Sit in the first eight rows toward the center aisle if you want to be picked, and further back if you emphatically do not.

The show runs in three set pieces with breakdowns between. The temple sequence is the best-known and comes first, which means people leave early and miss the plane. Do not do that. The last five minutes contain the biggest fireball in the park and the best physical stunt work of the day.
Heat is the real enemy. The seating is covered but open on the sides, and a 1pm show in July sits in still, thick air. The upper rows on the left get the most breeze and the earliest shade.
tips: Sit high and left. The upper left blocks get shade first, catch the cross breeze, and have a better view of the marketplace rooftop stunts than the center does.
Volunteers are chosen from people already seated when the doors open, not from the queue, so arriving early is the only way to be considered.
The pyrotechnics are loud enough that noise-reducing headphones are a reasonable call for sensitive kids; the concussive hits land around the twelve and twenty-five minute marks.
Never burn a Lightning Lane Multi Pass on this. The amphitheater holds two thousand people and standby seating almost never fills to the point of turning people away.

Repeat visitors: the between-scene patter changes performer to performer and the truck-fight cast improvises off the crowd, so the show is not word-for-word identical the way the projection shows are.
attractions.bestTime: The first performance of the day is the coolest and least crowded; the last is the most energetic.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue. Arrive 15 to 20 minutes before showtime for a good seat, 30 on a peak day.

faqs.q: How long is the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular?
faqs.a: About 30 minutes, plus 15 to 20 minutes of seating beforehand if you want a good spot. Budget roughly an hour of your day including walking to and from the amphitheater.

faqs.q: Is the show too loud or scary for young kids?
faqs.a: The explosions are genuinely loud and you feel them. Children who are comfortable with fireworks are usually fine; children who are not will struggle. There is nothing frightening about the content itself, only the volume and the pyrotechnics.

faqs.q: How do you get picked as a volunteer extra?
faqs.a: A casting director selects people from the seated audience before the show begins, favoring the front and center sections. You have to be in your seat early and visibly willing. Children are not selected; the volunteer roles are adults only.

faqs.q: Is there a height requirement?
faqs.a: None. Any age can attend, and infants can sit on a lap. The only practical restriction is tolerance for the noise level.

faqs.q: Does it get cancelled for rain?
faqs.a: The seating is covered but the stage is not fully protected, and heavy rain or lightning in the area will cancel a performance. If a show is cancelled the next scheduled one usually runs, so check the app rather than giving up on it.

attractions.name: For the First Time in Forever: A Frozen Sing-Along Celebration

scary.notes: The theater goes dark for the film clips and there is one loud snow-and-light effect near the end that catches small children by surprise. Otherwise this is the gentlest show in the park. Nothing chases anyone and nobody is in peril for more than a few seconds of clip footage.

accessibility.notes: Accessible seating is on the flat rear rows and the level side aisles, reached without steps from the main doors. Lyrics are projected on screen throughout, which makes this one of the most deaf-friendly shows in the park even without an interpreter. Sign language interpretation runs on a published schedule.

attractions.summary: An air-conditioned 30-minute sing-along in the Hyperion Theater with on-screen lyrics, two comic hosts and appearances by Anna, Elsa and Kristoff.
description: Two royal historians of Arendelle narrate the story of the first Frozen film in a fast, jokey, heavily fourth-wall-breaking style, with film clips on a large screen and lyrics projected so the audience can sing. Anna, Kristoff and Elsa appear on stage at intervals, and the show ends with the song you already know, a snow effect and a lighting cue.

The reason to see it is not the plot. It is that this is a thousand-plus-seat, air-conditioned, sit-down show in the middle of a park with brutal shade problems, and it runs roughly every hour. Treating it as a scheduled cooling break that happens to entertain your children is the correct way to use it.

The hosts carry the whole thing, and they are given real latitude to improvise. Two performances on the same day can differ by several minutes of material. Adults who arrive braced for a children's show are routinely surprised by how much of the comedy is aimed at them. A seasonal version of this show runs during the winter holidays; everything described here is the year-round production.
experience: The Hyperion Theater is large and it empties and refills between shows, so you queue in a covered outdoor holding area and then walk in en masse. If you arrive ten minutes before showtime you will get a seat; if you arrive twenty-five minutes early you get to choose it.

Once inside, the show opens with the two hosts, moves to a clip-and-song structure, and interleaves three live character appearances. Elsa's appearance is the visual set piece and uses the theater's lighting rig properly. The final number brings snow down over the front two-thirds of the house.

Sit center, about eight to twelve rows back. The character appearances happen on a raised platform behind the stage, and from the front rows you are craning upward; from the far sides the projected lyrics get keystoned and hard to read.
tips: The theater is the coldest room in the park. On a July afternoon this is a legitimate thirty-minute recovery, and nobody will look at you strangely for going in without children.
Sit in the center block from row eight back for the best angle on the character platform and the clearest read on the projected lyrics.
Snow falls over the front and center. If you have a child who wants to catch it, sit forward; if you have a stroller full of dry things, sit back.
The show is on the Lightning Lane Multi Pass list, which is almost always a waste. Standby seating rarely fills, and the theater turns over completely between shows.

Repeat visitors: the hosts riff on the crowd and on each other differently every performance, so the version you saw five years ago is not the version running now, even though the songs are unchanged.
attractions.bestTime: Early or mid-afternoon, when you actually want the air conditioning and the ride queues are at their worst.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue. Arrive 10 to 25 minutes before showtime depending on crowd level.

faqs.q: Do Anna and Elsa actually appear in person?
faqs.a: Yes. Anna, Elsa and Kristoff all appear live on stage during the show. It is not a meet and greet, so there are no photos or autographs, but you see them in person from your seat.

faqs.q: How long is the Frozen Sing-Along and how often does it run?
faqs.a: The show runs about 30 minutes and repeats through the day, generally around once an hour. Exact times are in the entertainment section of the app on the day you visit.

faqs.q: Is it only for small children?
faqs.a: No. The two host characters do a lot of dry, self-aware comedy aimed squarely at adults, and the show moves fast enough to hold teenagers. Plenty of adults go in for the air conditioning and end up enjoying it.

faqs.q: Is there a height or age requirement?
faqs.a: None at all. Infants can sit on a lap and there is no restriction of any kind. It is one of the few things at Hollywood Studios the whole family can do together regardless of size.

faqs.q: Should I use a Lightning Lane Multi Pass on it?
faqs.a: No. The theater seats well over a thousand people and clears completely between performances, so standby almost always works. Save your selections for Slinky Dog Dash, Tower of Terror or Rock 'n' Roller Coaster.

attractions.name: Vacation Fun: An Original Animated Short with Mickey & Minnie

scary.notes: A small theater that dims for a cartoon. There is nothing frightening in it. The only complaint young children have is that the room goes dark quickly at the start.

accessibility.notes: Step-free entry with bench seating and open floor space for wheelchairs at the back and sides. The theater is small enough that every seat has a clean sightline. The adjacent photo-op room is also fully step-free.

attractions.summary: A ten-minute cartoon program in the small Mickey Shorts Theater by Echo Lake, plus a walk-in photo set next door.
description: The Mickey Shorts Theater is a small, cool, almost always empty room that shows a compilation of the modern Mickey Mouse animated shorts strung together as a vacation story. It is not a headliner and it does not pretend to be. It is ten minutes of good animation in a chilled theater with almost no wait, which on a Florida afternoon is worth more than it sounds.

Next to the theater there is a walk-in photo set built to look like the inside of one of the cartoons, with an oversized prop you can stand in. It is free, PhotoPass photographers work it, and the queue for it is usually under five minutes.
The reason this entry exists in every serious touring plan is not the content, it is the arbitrage. Every attraction within two hundred feet of it has a forty-minute wait and this one has none.
tips: The theater turns over about every fifteen minutes, so a full house means a short wait, not a long one.
The photo set next door is a separate line from the theater. You can do one without the other.
It is the closest air-conditioned room to Star Tours, which makes it the natural place to park a group while one person rides.
Repeat visitors: the shorts program has been re-cut since the theater opened, so the running order is not the one you saw in 2020.
attractions.bestTime: Any time. It is functionally never busy, which is the whole point.
attractions.typicalWait: Zero to 15 minutes, dictated entirely by where the current showing is in its cycle.

attractions.name: Meet Olaf at Celebrity Spotlight

scary.notes: About as gentle as a character meet gets. Olaf is short, which is a genuine advantage with toddlers who find full-height costumed characters intimidating. The room is bright and quiet.

accessibility.notes: Step-free indoor queue with a level greeting area. Because the character is short, a seated guest is at conversation height rather than looking up, which makes for better photos from a wheelchair than most meets.

attractions.summary: An indoor, air-conditioned greeting with Olaf in the Celebrity Spotlight building on the Echo Lake side of the park.
description: Olaf greets guests indoors at Celebrity Spotlight, the small building on the far curve of Echo Lake. The queue is short, the room is cool, and the meet itself is unhurried compared with the character lines at Magic Kingdom.

Because the character is shorter than an adult, this is one of the easiest first character encounters for a nervous toddler. Children who back away from a full-height character will often walk straight up to this one.
PhotoPass photographers work the room and will take a photo on your own phone as well. It is a five-minute stop that produces one of the better photos of the day.
tips: Waits are longest in the hour right after the Frozen sing-along lets out. Go before a performance ends, not after.
The building is air conditioned and the queue is entirely indoors, so this is a legitimate place to cool down for fifteen minutes.
Ask the photographer to shoot low. Kneeling shots with a short character read much better than standing ones.
Repeat visitors: character assignments at this location have moved over the years, so confirm in the app rather than assuming the same character is there.
attractions.bestTime: Mid-morning, before the sing-along audiences start rotating through.
attractions.typicalWait: 10 to 30 minutes, spiking right after Frozen sing-along performances.

attractions.name: Jedi Training: Trials of the Temple
attractions.closedNote: The children's lightsaber training show near Star Tours stopped performing in 2020 and has not returned. There is no current equivalent at Walt Disney World.

scary.notes: Villain characters confronted children directly on stage at close range, and a meaningful number of young participants froze or cried at that moment. Historical entry only; the show no longer performs.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The show is not currently performing and the stage area near Star Tours is used for other purposes.

attractions.summary: The children's lightsaber training show staged near Star Tours; it has not performed since 2020 and has no replacement.
description: Children aged four to twelve signed up in the morning, were issued a robe and a training lightsaber, and performed a short choreographed routine on stage before facing a villain one at a time. Sign-ups filled within an hour of park opening and it was, for a decade, the single most emotionally memorable thing a small child could do at this park.

It stopped performing in 2020 and has not been reinstated. Nothing at Walt Disney World currently replaces it. Savi's Workshop in Galaxy's Edge is an adult-priced lightsaber build rather than a performance, and there is no on-stage equivalent.
People plan trips around things they remember, and this one still generates a large amount of search traffic every year. The honest answer is that it is gone and no return has been announced.
tips: Do not build a day around this. It has not run since 2020 and no return has been announced.
If your child wants a lightsaber experience, Savi's Workshop in Galaxy's Edge is the current option, but it is a build session at roughly $250 plus tax as of July 2026, not a show.
Galaxy's Edge roaming character encounters are the closest free substitute, and children in costume get noticeably more attention from the performers.
Repeat visitors: the sign-up desk that used to sit beside the Star Tours entrance is gone, so there is nowhere to ask about a waitlist.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.

attractions.name: The American Idol Experience
attractions.closedNote: Closed August 30, 2014. The theater it used has since been repurposed and the attraction has no successor.

scary.notes: A televised-style singing competition with an audience vote. Nothing about it frightened anyone. Historical entry only.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The attraction is not operating.

attractions.summary: A live singing competition where guests auditioned and audiences voted; it ran from 2009 to 2014 and has no successor.
description: Guests auditioned in the morning, a handful were selected, and the chosen singers performed in a full television-style theater with judges and an audience vote. The daily winner received a ticket that guaranteed a front-of-line audition for the actual television show, which gave the whole thing genuine stakes.
It closed in 2014 when the licensing agreement ended. The theater has since been used for other programming and nothing at Walt Disney World replaced the format.
It appears in this list because it is a common search for people returning after a decade away, and because the answer they need is simply that it is gone.
tips: This attraction closed in 2014. Do not plan around it.
The nearest live-performance equivalent now operating at this park is the Indiana Jones stunt show, which also uses volunteers from the audience.
If the appeal was participating rather than watching, the Citizens of Hollywood street performers pull guests into scenes daily and cost nothing.
Repeat visitors: the audition rooms behind the theater are not accessible and there is no backstage remnant to see.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.

attractions.name: Muppet*Vision 3D
attractions.closedNote: Closed in 2025 along with the surrounding Muppets Courtyard to make room for the Monstropolis project. Disney has not announced an opening date for what replaces it.

scary.notes: The 3D effects poked at the audience and the finale involved a loud practical explosion inside the theater, which startled small children reliably. Nothing in it was frightening in content. Historical entry only; the theater is closed.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The theater is closed and the surrounding courtyard is behind construction walls.

attractions.summary: The 1991 Muppets 3D film, one of the last projects Jim Henson worked on; closed in 2025 for the Monstropolis project.
description: For thirty-four years this was the best-loved thing in this corner of the park and the sharpest piece of comedy Disney has ever put in a theater. It combined a 3D film with practical in-theater effects, audio-animatronic characters in the balcony, a live performer, bubbles, water spray, and a genuinely destructive finale. Jim Henson worked on it before his death in 1990 and it opened in May 1991.

It closed in 2025 along with the Muppets Courtyard around it. The site is part of the Monstropolis project, which Disney has announced without giving an opening date. Anything you read that assigns it a year is speculation, not a Disney statement.

What this means in practice for a visitor today: Grand Avenue is a smaller land than it was, a section of it is behind construction walls, and the walkway through to Galaxy's Edge is narrower and noisier than it used to be. It is worth knowing before you arrive expecting to see the theater.
tips: The theater is closed and behind walls. There is nothing to see and no viewing area.
Grand Avenue is now a pass-through rather than a destination, so budget it as a two-minute walk to Galaxy's Edge, not a stop.
BaseLine Tap House and Mama Melrose's are still open in Grand Avenue and are unaffected by the construction walls.
Repeat visitors: the Muppets fountain and the surrounding courtyard architecture are inside the construction footprint, so the photo you are thinking of is no longer possible.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.

attractions.name: Honey, I Shrunk the Kids Movie Set Adventure
attractions.closedNote: Closed April 2016 with the rest of the Streets of America area. The site was redeveloped and the park currently has no dedicated outdoor playground.

scary.notes: An oversized playground with tunnels, a slide and water sprays. The enclosed tunnels were dark enough to worry a few small children. Historical entry only.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The play area no longer exists and the site has been redeveloped.

attractions.summary: The oversized backyard playground that ran from 1990 to 2016; the park has had no dedicated playground since it closed.
description: Giant blades of grass, a rope net made of spider web, an ant to climb on, a slide down a roll of film and water sprays that soaked whoever was standing in the wrong place. It was a straightforward playground scaled up, and for twenty-six years it was where parents let children run off energy in the middle of a park day.

It closed in April 2016 when the whole Streets of America section came down for Toy Story Land and Galaxy's Edge. Nothing at Hollywood Studios replaced it, and that absence is a real planning problem: this park now has no unstructured play space at all.
If your children need to move rather than queue, the practical substitutes are the interactive elements scattered through Galaxy's Edge, the open plaza in Toy Story Land, and the seated shows.
tips: The park has had no playground since 2016. Plan a midday break at the hotel pool if your children need to burn energy.
The closest thing to free play is the Play Disney Parks app content in Galaxy's Edge, which turns the land into a scavenger hunt.
Toy Story Land's oversized props are photo ops, not climbable. Cast members will ask children to get down.
Repeat visitors: the site sits under what is now the walkway between Grand Avenue and Toy Story Land, so there is nothing left to point at.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the play area is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the play area is permanently closed.

attractions.name: Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance

scary.notes: Two short free-fall drops at the end are the only physical thrill, and they are gentle compared with Tower of Terror. The real distress trigger for children is the middle section: you are marched off a transport by stormtroopers, held in a detention cell, and confronted at close range by a villain. Kids who dislike being told what to do by strangers in costume find that portion genuinely upsetting even though nothing happens to them.

accessibility.notes: The trackless ride vehicles include wheelchair-accessible units, but the attraction includes two standing pre-show rooms and a walking transfer between segments, so you must be able to stand and walk short distances or use a wheelchair through those rooms. The drop section requires transfer into a ride seat with a lap restraint.

attractions.summary: An eighteen-minute, four-part Star Wars ride combining a simulator, a trackless dark ride, a walkthrough and a drop; widely considered the best attraction Disney has built.
description: Rise of the Resistance is not a ride so much as a sequence of four rides wired together. You are recruited by the Resistance, board a transport shuttle, get captured by a Star Destroyer, escape through the ship aboard a trackless vehicle while stormtroopers and AT-AT walkers shoot at you, and finally drop out of the hull in an escape pod. It runs about eighteen minutes from the first pre-show to the exit, which is roughly three times the length of a normal Disney dark ride.

It opened in December 2019 and it changed what people expect from this park. The scale is the point: the hangar bay you walk into holds a full-size vehicle and around fifty stormtroopers, and the ride's most-photographed moment is a room you walk through rather than ride past. Very little of the budget went into things you would notice on a POV video, which is why it holds up in person far better than it does on a phone screen.

It is also the most breakdown-prone major attraction at Walt Disney World. Four ride systems in series means four things that can stop, and it goes down for a stretch on most days. That is not a reason to skip it; it is a reason to ride it early, when the day's first fault has not happened yet and the recovery queue has not formed.
experience: The queue winds through a rock formation and into a Resistance base with a full-size starfighter parked in it. You get a briefing from a hologram, then load into a transport shuttle. The shuttle is a simulator with windows; there is no motion base drama here, just a good view and a very effective moment when the ship is captured.

The doors open and you march out into the Star Destroyer hangar. This is the set piece everyone remembers and it is the one part where you should walk slowly and look up. Then a short interrogation scene, then you board the trackless vehicle. From there the ride runs about five minutes through corridors, a cannon bay, an escape and a chase, with your vehicle spinning, reversing and occasionally being lifted.

The finish is two short free-falls of maybe a story and a half each. They are startling rather than intense, and there is an on-ride photo at the second one. If you want the photo to be good, the camera is above and slightly to the right of the escape pod door.
tips: This is the one attraction here that justifies buying a Lightning Lane Single Pass. If you buy exactly one Single Pass all day, buy it for this.
Ride it in the first hour if you are going standby. The queue does not get shorter later, and a mid-morning breakdown adds an hour to everyone's plan.
The trackless vehicles seat two rows of four. Ask for row one, right side, for the best view into the cannon bay sequence.
If the ride stops mid-experience, cast members will either restart it or walk you out with a re-entry pass. Take the pass and come back late; do not argue for a re-ride on the spot.

Repeat visitors: the hangar bay scene has a different stormtrooper deployment depending on which shuttle group you are with, and the interrogation-room villain varies. The ride is more variable than its reputation suggests.
attractions.bestTime: First 60 minutes of the day, or the last hour before close if the ride has been running reliably.
attractions.typicalWait: 60 to 120 minutes for most of the day, longer after any downtime. Under 45 only at open and close.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Rise of the Resistance?
faqs.a: 40 inches. It is measured at the entrance with shoes on, and children who clear are given an all-day wristband so they are not re-measured at other attractions. Rider switch is available if one child in your party is too short.

faqs.q: Is Rise of the Resistance scary?
faqs.a: For adults, no. For children, the frightening part is not the two small drops at the end but the middle section, where stormtroopers march you off a transport and a villain confronts your group at close range. Children who are sensitive to being singled out find that harder than any coaster.

faqs.q: How big are the drops?
faqs.a: Two short free-falls, each roughly a story and a half, at the very end of the ride. They are nothing like Tower of Terror. Most people who dislike drop rides can handle these.

faqs.q: Does Rise of the Resistance still use a virtual queue?
faqs.a: No. The virtual queue was retired and the attraction now runs on standby plus Lightning Lane Single Pass. You can walk up and join the standby line whenever you like.

faqs.q: Why does it break down so often?
faqs.a: The attraction chains four separate ride systems together, so a fault in any one of them stops the whole experience. It goes down at some point on most operating days. Ride early, and if you are evacuated mid-ride take the re-entry pass you are offered.

faqs.q: How long does the whole experience take?
faqs.a: About 18 minutes from the first pre-show to the exit, and that is after the standby queue. Plan for it to consume a genuine chunk of your morning even with a Lightning Lane.

attractions.name: Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run

scary.notes: Almost nothing here frightens children. The cockpit is bright, the crew of six sits together, and the threat is abstract. What it does do is make people queasy: a six-person cabin on a motion base with a wraparound screen, plus the fact that a bad pilot produces a much rougher ride than a good one.

accessibility.notes: You must transfer into a fixed cockpit seat; the cabins are compact and the engineer seats in the back row are the tightest. Guests who cannot use their hands can ride as an engineer and let a companion handle the controls. The queue includes a long ramp but no steps.

attractions.summary: Six guests fly the Millennium Falcon together as pilots, gunners and engineers, with the flight quality depending entirely on who gets the pilot seats.
description: You board the Falcon in crews of six and are assigned one of three roles: two pilots at the front controlling left-right and up-down, two gunners in the middle firing at targets, two engineers in the back mashing buttons when the ship takes damage. Everyone can see the same forward view through the cockpit windows, and everyone's inputs genuinely affect what happens on screen and how much the cabin lurches.

The queue is the best-built environment in the park. It runs through a cantina-adjacent alley, past a workshop, and then into the Falcon herself, including the corridor and the chess table you have seen in the films. Even if you have no interest in the ride, walk the standby queue once for the set.

The catch with a group ride is that the experience is unevenly distributed. Pilots have the most to do and the most fun, gunners have a straightforward job, engineers are essentially passengers with buttons. If your party is six people you control the assignment. If you are a party of two, you get whatever is left.
experience: You are grouped in the queue and assigned roles by a cast member near the boarding gate. Ask for pilot and you will sometimes get it; ask with a child who wants to fly and your odds improve considerably. Roles are assigned per cabin, so a party of six can request the whole crew configuration.

The flight is about four and a half minutes: a launch, a canyon run, a cargo grab, a fight, and a return. The cabin pitches and rolls with the flying, so a crew of two flailing pilots produces a much rougher and much funnier ride than a competent pair. Crashing into things is essentially free and does not end the ride.

As a pilot, the left seat controls up and down, the right seat controls left and right. That split is not obvious and it is the single reason most first-time crews fly badly. Sort it out in the boarding corridor before the doors close.
tips: Left pilot handles vertical, right pilot handles horizontal. Say that out loud to your co-pilot before you sit down and your flight will be twice as good.
Single rider is offered and it is the fastest queue in the park, often twenty minutes when standby is sixty. You will almost always be seated as an engineer.
Riding as an engineer with a motion-sensitive stomach is worse, not better, because you are furthest from the window. If you get queasy, ask for a gunner seat.
The standby queue is the attraction as much as the ride is. Skipping it with a Lightning Lane means missing the Falcon corridor entirely; do standby at least once.

Repeat visitors: your flight performance is tracked and a bad flight follows you into the Play Disney Parks app as a reputation hit with the in-land factions, which changes some app interactions in the land.
attractions.bestTime: During the nighttime show, when a large share of the park moves to Sunset Boulevard.
attractions.typicalWait: 35 to 75 minutes standby; single rider frequently under 25.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run?
faqs.a: 38 inches, which is two inches lower than Rise of the Resistance and Star Tours. It is the most accessible of the three Star Wars rides for smaller children.

faqs.q: Can you choose to be a pilot?
faqs.a: You can ask, and cast members will often accommodate a child or a party that requests it, but assignments are made per cabin and are not guaranteed. A full party of six can effectively choose all three role pairs.

faqs.q: Does Smugglers Run make you motion sick?
faqs.a: Some people, yes, though generally less than Star Tours. The cabin motion follows the pilots' inputs, so a chaotic crew makes for a rougher ride. Sitting as a gunner in the middle row is the mildest position.

faqs.q: Is there a single rider line?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is one of the best-value single rider queues at Walt Disney World, regularly half the standby wait or less. The trade-off is that single riders are usually seated as engineers.

faqs.q: Is it scary for young kids?
faqs.a: Rarely. The cockpit is bright, your whole group sits together, and there are no drops or darkness. The main complaints from small children are the volume and the shaking, not fear.

attractions.name: Savi's Workshop: Handbuilt Lightsabers

scary.notes: The room dims and the presentation has a solemn, ceremonial tone that occasionally reads as spooky to very young children. Nothing jumps out and nobody is threatened. The bigger risk is boredom for a child under six during the talking portions.

accessibility.notes: The workshop is step-free with standing-height build stations, and a cast member will lower a station or bring parts to a seated guest. The room is small and dim, and the group stands close together for about twenty minutes, which is worth knowing if crowding is a problem.

attractions.summary: A twenty-minute paid ceremony where you assemble a custom lightsaber hilt from four design themes; around $250 plus tax as of July 2026.
description: Savi's Workshop is a paid experience rather than an attraction, and it is the most expensive thing a guest can do inside Hollywood Studios on an ordinary day. You reserve a slot, you pay roughly $250 plus tax as of July 2026, and you spend twenty minutes in a dim workshop building a lightsaber hilt from a tray of parts under the direction of a performer.

The build itself is real in a limited sense. You choose one of four design themes, then select from a tray of hilt components within that theme, and physically screw the pieces together. The blade, a metal hilt, a carry case and a belt clip come with it. It is a substantial physical object, not a toy, and it comes apart and reassembles.

Whether it is worth the money depends entirely on whether you want the object or the moment. As a souvenir, it is expensive but genuinely well made and it holds resale value. As an experience, twenty minutes is short and the ceremony leans heavily on the performer's ability to sell it. A great host makes it the best twenty minutes of the trip; an indifferent one makes it a retail transaction with candles.
experience: You check in at a small door in the Black Spire Outpost marketplace and wait in an anteroom. Groups are around fourteen builders, each allowed one guest to accompany them, and the room is tight. A performer opens the session with a short piece of theater and then introduces the four hilt themes.

After you choose a theme, a tray comes out with parts: emitter, sleeve, pommel, activation plate and a kyber crystal in a color you select. You build in stages, following the performer's pacing, and there is a genuinely well-staged moment at the end when the whole room activates the blades together in a dark room. That moment is what people pay for.

The whole thing runs about twenty minutes. Afterward you carry the finished saber in a hard case, which is bulky. If you are riding anything with a lap restraint for the rest of the day, plan on a locker or a resort delivery.
tips: Book the earliest slot of the day. The room is coolest, the performers are freshest, and you avoid carrying a large case around for eight hours.
Only the builder gets a saber; each builder may bring one guest into the room. A family of four with two builders needs two reservations.
Reservations open on the app and by phone well in advance and the good slots go quickly, but cancellations release constantly. Check the day before.
The hard case does not fit in a ride locker at some attractions. Ask about package delivery to the front of the park, or to your Disney resort if you are staying on property.
Repeat visitors: the four hilt themes have not changed, but the individual parts within each tray have been revised, so a second build produces a genuinely different hilt rather than a duplicate.
attractions.bestTime: The first reservation slot of the day, before the marketplace fills and before you are carrying anything else.
attractions.typicalWait: Reservation only. No standby, no walk-up availability on most days.

faqs.q: How much does Savi's Workshop cost?
faqs.a: Around $250 plus tax as of July 2026 for one builder and one lightsaber. Prices have risen roughly annually since it opened, so treat that as a floor rather than a fixed figure and check the app when you book.

faqs.q: Do you need a reservation for Savi's Workshop?
faqs.a: Effectively yes. Reservations open in advance through the Disney app and by phone, and walk-up availability is rare. Cancellations do release, so it is worth checking the app the day before and the morning of.

faqs.q: Can more than one person build a lightsaber in the same session?
faqs.a: Yes, but each builder needs their own paid reservation. Each builder may bring one non-building guest into the room to watch, and that guest does not pay.

faqs.q: Is there an age or height requirement?
faqs.a: No height requirement. Children can build, though the assembly involves small threaded parts and most families find a child under about seven needs an adult's hands. The talking portions test the patience of very young children.

faqs.q: Can you take the lightsaber on rides and on a plane?
faqs.a: The hilt disassembles and the blade detaches, which is what makes it packable. It does not fit in every ride locker assembled, so plan to use package pickup at the front of the park. For flights, pack it in checked luggage.

attractions.name: Droid Depot

scary.notes: A bright workshop with a parts conveyor. There is nothing frightening about it at all, and it is one of the easiest experiences in the land for a child who found Rise of the Resistance overwhelming.

accessibility.notes: Step-free throughout with a bench-height build counter that works from a seated position. The parts conveyor is at standing height but cast members will pull parts down on request.

attractions.summary: A build-your-own remote-controlled droid workshop where you pick parts off a conveyor and assemble a working unit in about fifteen minutes.
description: Droid Depot is the cheaper and more child-friendly of the two build experiences in Galaxy's Edge. You choose a chassis, pull parts off a moving conveyor, assemble them at a counter with a cast member's help, and walk out with a remote-controlled droid that reacts to elements placed around the land.

It costs meaningfully less than a lightsaber build and takes about fifteen minutes rather than twenty. The result is a real toy that works at home, and the interactive behavior inside the land is the part people underrate: droids chirp and react near specific doorways and vehicles in Black Spire Outpost.
The workshop also sells personality chips and accessories separately, which is where the cost creeps up. It is easy to walk in expecting one price and walk out having spent half again as much.
tips: Reservations are recommended but walk-up slots open regularly, especially in the first hour and the last two hours of the day.
Carry the droid in the box while you tour. The unpacked droid does not survive being jostled in a bag, and the boxes are awkward on rides.
Take the finished droid to the doorways around the marketplace and the docking bay; it reacts to hidden transmitters and that is the free part of the experience most people never try.
Repeat visitors: personality chips bought on a previous trip still work with a new build, so a second droid does not need a second chip.
attractions.bestTime: First hour of the day for the shortest wait, or late evening when reservations are released.
attractions.typicalWait: Reservation-driven; walk-up waits are usually 10 to 30 minutes when available.

attractions.name: Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities

scary.notes: A dim antiquities shop with a large animatronic proprietor behind the counter who moves and speaks. A few small children are startled by him the first time he turns his head. Otherwise it is completely benign.

accessibility.notes: Step-free with narrow aisles that get congested at peak times; a large ECV is a genuine squeeze in the back rooms. The lighting is deliberately low throughout.

attractions.summary: A dim curiosity shop run by a full-size animatronic proprietor, with more genuine set dressing than most walkthrough attractions in the park.
description: Nominally this is a store. Functionally it is the best free walkthrough in Galaxy's Edge, because the room is packed with props referencing the films and the shopkeeper behind the counter is a full-size animatronic who moves, speaks and reacts to a soundtrack of haggling.

The shelves are worth ten slow minutes even if you never buy anything. Ancient weapons, holocrons, a carbonite slab, jars of things nobody explains. Nearly everything on display corresponds to something specific, and the staff are trained to explain items if asked.
It is also the coolest indoor room in the land other than the cantina, which makes it a reasonable place to stand still for a few minutes on a brutal afternoon without paying for a drink.
tips: Go around the left side of the counter and look behind the shopkeeper. The best props are in the back alcove that most people walk past.
The animatronic runs a repeating cycle of a few minutes; wait for a full loop if you want to hear him actually speak rather than mutter.
It is a genuine air-conditioned break with no purchase required, unlike the cantina next door.
Repeat visitors: the legacy lightsaber hilts sold here change stock periodically and a hilt available on one trip may not be on the shelf the next.
attractions.bestTime: Midday, when you want indoor air and the queues outside are at their worst.
attractions.typicalWait: No wait. Occasional entry metering at peak, rarely more than five minutes.

attractions.name: Star Wars: Datapad in Play Disney Parks

scary.notes: A phone-based scavenger game played while walking around the land. There is nothing here to frighten anyone of any age.

accessibility.notes: Entirely self-paced and playable from a seated position anywhere in the land, though some scan targets are mounted above standing eye level and need a companion to reach. Requires a phone, park wifi and a battery that will survive it.

attractions.summary: A free phone-based layer over Galaxy's Edge that lets you hack panels, scan crates, translate signs and pick a side between factions.
description: The Play Disney Parks app turns Galaxy's Edge into a playable space. You can point your phone at crates to scan their contents, hack door panels, tune into ship-to-ship transmissions, translate the alien signage that is written throughout the land, and take on jobs from the three in-land factions.

It is completely free, it is the single best thing to do in this land while waiting for a Lightning Lane return window, and the overwhelming majority of guests never open it. That is a shame, because a fair amount of design work in Black Spire Outpost only becomes visible through it.
The catch is battery. Running the app with location services and the camera active for an hour will visibly drain a phone, and there are few outlets in the land.
tips: Download the app and the Galaxy's Edge content pack before you arrive. Downloading it on park wifi at the entrance wastes twenty minutes.
Choosing a faction early changes which jobs you get offered, and your flight performance on Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run feeds into your standing with them.
Bring a battery pack. An hour of scanning will take a phone from full to roughly half.
Repeat visitors: your progress persists between trips on the same account, so a partially finished job list from a previous visit is still waiting.
attractions.bestTime: While waiting for a Lightning Lane return window or a dining reservation inside the land.
attractions.typicalWait: No wait. Play at your own pace anywhere in Galaxy's Edge.

attractions.name: Galaxy's Edge Character Encounters

scary.notes: The villain encounters are deliberately confrontational. Stormtroopers question guests, block paths and single people out, and a specific dark-side character stares down children on purpose. Plenty of small kids find that genuinely upsetting, and plenty of others think it is the highlight of the trip.

accessibility.notes: Roaming encounters on flat pavement with no formal queue, so a wheelchair user can approach from any direction. Performers routinely come down to seated eye level. There is no shade in most of the encounter areas.

attractions.summary: Unscheduled roaming appearances by Rey, Chewbacca, Kylo Ren, stormtroopers and Vi Moradi throughout Black Spire Outpost.
description: There is no character meet building in Galaxy's Edge and no posted schedule. Instead performers appear in the streets of Black Spire Outpost, work an area for fifteen or twenty minutes, and move on. Rey and Chewbacca tend to appear near the resistance side of the land, stormtroopers patrol the marketplace, and the dark-side characters stage near the docking bay.

Because they roam and improvise, these are the best character interactions at Walt Disney World. Stormtroopers will interrogate a guest about the contents of a shopping bag. Rey will duck behind a crate to hide from a patrol. None of it is scripted the way a meet-and-greet line is.
The trade-off is unpredictability. You cannot plan around them, and there is no queue to join. If seeing a specific character matters, you spend time walking the land and getting lucky.
tips: Encounters are most frequent in the first two hours after opening and again in the last two hours of the night. The middle of the afternoon is thin.
Children in Star Wars costume get pulled into bits far more often than adults do. That is by design, and it is the cheapest way to guarantee an interaction.
PhotoPass photographers shadow the roaming performers. Look for the photographer to find the character rather than the other way around.
Repeat visitors: the marketplace alleyways behind the main path are used as staging routes, so standing near the ends of them puts you first in front of a character who is about to appear.
attractions.bestTime: First two hours after opening, or after dark when the land's lighting makes the photos far better.
attractions.typicalWait: No formal queue. Ad-hoc groups form around performers and clear within a few minutes.

attractions.name: Slinky Dog Dash

scary.notes: A family coaster with two launches and a handful of airtime hills, all outdoors in daylight. There is nothing dark and nothing that jumps out. The drops produce a real lift out of the seat, so a first-time coaster rider at exactly 38 inches will feel it, but this is the correct first big coaster for most kids.

accessibility.notes: You must transfer into a coaster car with a lap bar; the cars are narrow and the step over the side is fairly high. The queue is long, entirely outdoors and mostly unshaded, which is a genuine problem for anyone who cannot stand in heat.

attractions.summary: A two-launch outdoor family coaster over the top of Toy Story Land, and the hardest ride in this park to get on without a plan.
description: Slinky Dog Dash is a family coaster with two launch sections, a run of low airtime hills and a layout that climbs above the rest of Toy Story Land. It is not fast by coaster standards and it does not invert, but it is genuinely fun, and it is the ride at Hollywood Studios with the worst wait-to-length ratio in the park: two minutes of ride behind an hour of queue is routine.

The reason is capacity. The trains are short and the layout is long, so the ride simply cannot absorb the demand it generates, and it draws from every part of the family market at once. Adults ride it, teenagers ride it, and children clear the 38-inch stick years before they clear 48.
It opened with Toy Story Land in June 2018 and it has not gotten less busy since. Treat it as the ride you plan the morning around, not something you fit in later.
experience: The queue is the worst in the park: long, switchbacked, mostly in direct sun, with only intermittent canopies. On a July afternoon the standby line is a real health consideration, not just an inconvenience. Bring water, bring a fan, and reconsider standby entirely between noon and four.

The ride itself opens with a lift, a first drop through the land, a launch section that snaps you forward, a swooping turn over the top of the queue, a second launch, and a run of small hills into the brakes. The best airtime is on the hills after the second launch, and the best view of the land is on the high right-hand turn.

Sit in the back row. The back car gets pulled over each crest and produces noticeably more lift than the front. The front is better for the view and for a child who wants to see where they are going, but the back is the better ride.
tips: Back row for airtime, front row for the view. Ask at the load platform and the wait for the back is usually one or two extra trains.
