This should be your first Lightning Lane Multi Pass selection of the day, ahead of Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster, because the standby alternative is so much worse.
If you are going standby, go at rope drop or in the last 45 minutes before close. Both routinely produce waits under 25 minutes; the middle of the day does not.
The queue has almost no shade. If someone in your group is heat-sensitive, this is the single line at Hollywood Studios where you should use rider switch and split up rather than all stand in it.
Repeat visitors: night rides are meaningfully better. The land's lighting turns the layout into something worth looking at, and the second launch reads much faster in the dark.
attractions.bestTime: Rope drop or the final 45 minutes of the night. Night rides are better; morning rides are shorter waits.
attractions.typicalWait: 60 to 110 minutes through the middle of the day, dropping to 20 to 35 at open and close.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Slinky Dog Dash?
faqs.a: 38 inches. It is the lowest height requirement of any coaster at Hollywood Studios and one of the reasons the line is so long. Rider switch is available for parties with a child under the limit.

faqs.q: Is Slinky Dog Dash scary?
faqs.a: Not particularly. It runs entirely outdoors in daylight, has no inversions, no dark sections and no big drop. The two launches are brisk and the airtime hills lift you out of the seat, which is enough to thrill a first-time coaster rider without frightening them.

faqs.q: Why is the wait for Slinky Dog Dash always so long?
faqs.a: Low capacity meeting very broad appeal. The trains are short, the circuit is long, and it is the only major coaster in the park that most children can ride. The queue does not meaningfully shorten during the day, only at open and close.

faqs.q: Is it worth a Lightning Lane Multi Pass?
faqs.a: Yes, and it should usually be your first selection at this park. The standby alternative is a long, hot, unshaded queue, and the ride is short enough that an hour in line feels like a poor trade.

faqs.q: Should I ride Slinky Dog Dash at night?
faqs.a: If you can manage only one ride, do it after dark. The lighting package on the land makes the layout far more interesting and the launches feel faster when you cannot see what is coming.

attractions.name: Toy Story Midway Mania!

scary.notes: Bright, indoors, slow, and structured as a carnival. There is nothing frightening in it. The vehicles rotate between screens, which occasionally bothers guests prone to motion sickness, but children are essentially never scared here.

accessibility.notes: There are wheelchair-accessible vehicles that load without transferring, and the shooter is mounted so it can be used from a seated position. Guests with limited grip strength can ask for a modified spring-action shooter that requires less pull force.

attractions.summary: A 3D interactive shooting ride through five carnival games, with a scoreboard that turns the whole family competitive within about ninety seconds.
description: You wear 3D glasses, sit in a car with a spring-loaded shooter, and rotate between five screens playing carnival midway games: throwing rings at aliens, cracking plates, popping balloons with darts, and so on. Your score displays on the dashboard next to your partner's, and that is the entire hook. It opened in 2008 and it works as well now as it did then.

The ride is genuinely skill-based, which almost nothing else at Walt Disney World is. Learning where the high-value targets hide is the difference between a score of 90,000 and a score of 250,000, and people who ride it repeatedly get dramatically better at it.

It is also one of the few attractions at this park with no height requirement, indoors, air conditioned, and suitable for grandparents and toddlers in the same vehicle. That combination is why it holds a long line all day despite being nearly twenty years old.
experience: The queue is themed as an oversized toy box, with a large animatronic ringmaster near the boarding area. Standby routes you through more of it than Lightning Lane does, and there are hidden gags in the boxes worth looking at.

In the car, pull the string quickly and repeatedly rather than aiming carefully. Volume beats precision on most screens, with two exceptions: the dart-and-balloon screen rewards hitting specific balloons that open into higher-value targets, and the plate-smashing screen has a large center target that pays far more than the plates around it.
Cars seat four, in pairs back to back. Your score is compared against the person beside you, not the pair behind. If you want a fair contest, seat the two competitive people together.
tips: Fire fast and often. The shooter has no ammunition limit and rate of fire beats accuracy on four of the five screens.
On the balloon screen, hit the balloons that reveal secondary targets behind them rather than clearing the easy ones; that is where the score separation happens.
Aim for the volcano on the plate screen and the center of the ring toss target. Both hide multipliers that most riders never find.
It is one of only two significant attractions here with no height requirement, so it is the natural anchor for a day with a toddler.

Repeat visitors: the practice screen before the first real game does not count toward your score, so use it to check your shooter is firing properly. A jammed shooter can be swapped if you flag it before the ride starts.
attractions.bestTime: First 30 minutes of the day, or during the nighttime show when the crowd shifts to Sunset Boulevard.
attractions.typicalWait: 40 to 75 minutes midday; under 30 at open and in the last hour.

faqs.q: Is there a height requirement for Toy Story Midway Mania?
faqs.a: No. Any guest who can sit up with an adult can ride, including infants. With Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway it is one of only two headliner-level attractions at Hollywood Studios with no height stick.

faqs.q: How do you get a high score on Toy Story Midway Mania?
faqs.a: Fire continuously rather than aiming carefully, and learn the hidden high-value targets: the balloons that reveal secondary targets, the volcano on the plate screen, and the center of the ring toss. Practiced riders score two to three times what first-timers do.

faqs.q: Is Toy Story Midway Mania scary?
faqs.a: No. It is bright, indoors, slow-moving and framed as a carnival. It is the safest choice in this park for a child who is anxious about rides.

faqs.q: Does the ride make you motion sick?
faqs.a: Occasionally. The vehicles spin to face each screen, and a small number of guests find the rotation combined with the 3D uncomfortable. It is far milder than Star Tours or Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run.

faqs.q: Can wheelchair users ride without transferring?
faqs.a: Yes. Accessible vehicles load directly and the shooter can be operated from a seated position. Ask a cast member at the entrance and you will be routed to the appropriate loading area.

attractions.name: Alien Swirling Saucers

scary.notes: A whip-style flat ride that swings you side to side under a canopy. Nothing is dark, nothing drops and nothing jumps out. The only issue is the lateral force, which pushes riders into each other hard enough to bruise a shoulder if you sit badly.

accessibility.notes: You transfer into a small bench vehicle with a lap bar and a fairly high step in. The lateral swinging is significant, so a guest with a back, neck or shoulder condition should skip this even though it looks tame from the queue.

attractions.summary: A short whip-style flat ride under a canopy, with the lowest height requirement in the park at 32 inches and the shortest ride time.
description: Alien Swirling Saucers is a carnival whip ride dressed up as a toy playset. Saucers tow small rocket cars around two swirling patterns while music plays, and the whole cycle lasts about ninety seconds. It is the ride at Hollywood Studios with the lowest height requirement, at 32 inches, which is why families with toddlers gravitate to it.

It is also, honestly, the weakest attraction Disney has built in this park in twenty years. The ride time is short, the capacity is low, the queue is outdoors, and the experience is a flat ride you could find at a county fair with better theming. On any day where the posted wait exceeds about 25 minutes, it is a poor use of your time.

That said, if you have a three-year-old who cannot ride Slinky Dog Dash, this is a real ride they can do, and their reaction to it will be out of all proportion to the machine. Judge it on that basis and it earns its place.
experience: The queue runs under a partial canopy and is one of the shadier lines in Toy Story Land, which is faint praise but true. Loading is slow because each car takes one adult and one child or two smaller adults, and the operators have to check every lap bar individually.

The ride itself swings you outward hard on the turns. Sit on the outside of the bench if you want the force and the inside if you would rather be the one doing the crushing; whoever sits outside gets pressed into the wall of the car repeatedly.
It is over quickly. The full cycle including load and unload runs about four minutes, of which ninety seconds is motion.
tips: 32 inches is the lowest height requirement in the entire park, which makes this the first real ride many toddlers can do at Hollywood Studios.
Sit inside, not outside, if you have a shoulder or neck issue. The lateral force is stronger than the ride looks.
Never use a Lightning Lane Multi Pass here. The ride is ninety seconds long and there are four attractions in this park where that selection is worth ten times more.
Waits are shortest during the first hour and during the nighttime show, and it is the only ride in Toy Story Land where the last thirty minutes of the night are usually a walk-on.
Repeat visitors: the ride uses two different swirl patterns and the operator selects one per cycle, so a second ride is genuinely a different path around the pad.
attractions.bestTime: Last 30 minutes of the night, when it routinely drops to a walk-on.
attractions.typicalWait: 25 to 50 minutes midday, which is far more than it is worth; under 15 late.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Alien Swirling Saucers?
faqs.a: 32 inches, the lowest of any attraction at Hollywood Studios. Rider switch is available if you have a child below that.

faqs.q: How long is the ride?
faqs.a: About 90 seconds of motion, roughly four minutes including loading and unloading. It is the shortest ride at the park by a clear margin.

faqs.q: Is Alien Swirling Saucers worth the wait?
faqs.a: Honestly, not above about 25 minutes. It is a well-themed county fair whip ride with low capacity. If you have a toddler who cannot ride anything else, it is worth it to them; for adults alone it is not.

faqs.q: Is it rough?
faqs.a: Rougher than it looks. The lateral swing presses the outside rider firmly into the side of the car on every turn, and guests with neck, back or shoulder problems should skip it.

faqs.q: Can two adults ride together?
faqs.a: Yes, though the bench is narrow and two full-size adults are a tight fit. Most parties pair one adult with one child.

attractions.name: Toy Story Land Character Meets

scary.notes: Outdoor daytime greetings with cast members managing the pace. Nothing here frightens anyone, though the full-height characters can be intimidating to a toddler at close range in the same way any costumed character is.

accessibility.notes: Flat outdoor queues with partial shade and no steps. There is very little seating nearby, and the pavement radiates heat badly in the afternoon, which matters for anyone who cannot stand for long.

attractions.summary: Outdoor greetings with Woody, Jessie and Buzz Lightyear near the entrance to Toy Story Land, with short queues most of the day.
description: Woody and Jessie greet together near the entrance arch, and Buzz Lightyear greets separately a short walk away. These are straightforward outdoor character meets with PhotoPass photographers, and the queues are usually far shorter than the equivalent lines at Magic Kingdom.

The land is scaled as though you have been shrunk to toy size, so the characters are staged against oversized props, which makes for better photographs than a plain backdrop. Buzz in particular is set up in a spot that photographs well from a low angle.
There is no indoor waiting and no shade to speak of, which is the whole problem with these meets. In July, a twenty-minute wait in this queue is genuinely unpleasant.
tips: Go in the first hour or after dark. The midday sun on this pavement is the worst in the park and there is no canopy over the queues.
Woody and Jessie greet together, so one queue gets you two characters. Buzz is a separate line.
Character sets rotate through the day with breaks. If a queue is roped off, a cast member will usually tell you the return time rather than the wait.
Repeat visitors: the greeting positions moved when the land's walkways were reworked, so the spots you remember from 2018 are not necessarily where they stand now.
attractions.bestTime: First hour of the day or after sunset; midday queues here are hot and shadeless.
attractions.typicalWait: 10 to 30 minutes per character, shortest right at opening.

attractions.name: Studio Backlot Tour
attractions.closedNote: Closed September 27, 2014. The backlot it toured was cleared and the land now holds Toy Story Land and part of Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge.

scary.notes: The canyon segment involved a large fire effect and a water surge directed at the tram, which startled children reliably. Historical entry only; the attraction no longer operates.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The attraction is not operating and its route has been built over.

attractions.summary: The tram tour of the working backlot that ran from the park's 1989 opening until 2014; the route is now Toy Story Land and Galaxy's Edge.
description: When this park opened in 1989 it was a functioning production facility, and the Backlot Tour was the tour of it. A tram carried guests past costume and prop warehouses, through a special effects canyon with a staged flash flood and fire, and along a street of facades used for filming. Over the years the working studio shrank, the tour was cut down, and by the end it was a twenty-minute shadow of the original.
It closed in September 2014. The land it occupied became Toy Story Land and part of Galaxy's Edge, so nothing of the route survives.

It is included here because it is a common search from returning visitors, and because the park's shift away from a working-studio identity is the single biggest change between a 1990s visit and a 2026 one.
tips: This attraction closed in 2014 and the route is built over. There is nothing to see.
The park no longer functions as a production studio in any visible way, so do not plan a day around behind-the-scenes content.
Walt Disney Presents in Animation Courtyard is the closest surviving thing to the park's original studio-history programming.
Repeat visitors: the water tower and a handful of facade elements from the backlot era are gone, but the Chinese Theatre and the Echo Lake structures are original.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.

attractions.name: Lights, Motors, Action! Extreme Stunt Show
attractions.closedNote: Closed April 2, 2016. The stadium was demolished and the site is now part of Toy Story Land.

scary.notes: Extremely loud: engines, gunfire effects, explosions and a jet ski sequence in an open stadium. It was the loudest attraction the park ever had. Historical entry only.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The stadium was demolished and the attraction does not operate.

attractions.summary: The car stunt stadium show that ran from 2005 to 2016; the site was demolished and became Toy Story Land.
description: A five-thousand-seat stadium staged a European street chase with cars, motorcycles and a jet ski, complete with a car that drove on two wheels and a stunt driver set on fire. It was imported from the Disneyland Paris version and it was, by a distance, the loudest and largest-scale show this park has ever run.
It closed in April 2016 and the stadium came down to make room for Toy Story Land, which opened in 2018 on part of the footprint.

The Indiana Jones stunt show is the only live stunt production left at Hollywood Studios, and it is a very different and much smaller thing. If you remember this show and are wondering whether the park still does anything like it, the honest answer is no.
tips: This show closed in 2016 and the stadium no longer exists.
The Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular is the surviving stunt show at this park and is worth your time, but it is a fraction of the scale.
If big automotive stunt work is what you are after, this style of show no longer runs at any Walt Disney World park.
Repeat visitors: the stadium sat roughly where Slinky Dog Dash's queue and the Toy Story Land entrance are now, which is why that corner of the park feels so much more open than it used to.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the show is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the show is permanently closed.

attractions.name: The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror

scary.notes: This is the most frightening attraction at Walt Disney World and it earns that from three separate directions: a genuinely creepy queue and lobby, a dark and unsettling ride-through section, and then a sequence of free-falls that pull you up against the harness. Children who clear 40 inches are frequently not ready for it emotionally, and plenty of adults who ride coasters happily will not ride this twice. The drop pattern is randomized, so you cannot brace for the next one.

accessibility.notes: You must transfer into a bench seat with a seatbelt; there is no wheelchair-accessible vehicle. The pre-show library is a standing room and the boiler room queue involves a long walk over uneven floor. Guests with back, neck or heart conditions should not ride, and the warning here is not boilerplate.

attractions.summary: A 199-foot drop ride inside a decaying hotel, with a randomized drop sequence and the best queue and pre-show Disney has ever built.
description: The Hollywood Tower Hotel opened in 1994 and it remains the finest piece of environmental storytelling at Walt Disney World. Before you get anywhere near a drop, you walk through an overgrown garden, a dust-covered lobby frozen mid-check-in, a library where a television plays a black-and-white introduction, and a boiler room. Every one of those spaces is built to a standard that most modern attractions do not attempt.

The ride itself is a vertical motion system in a service elevator that moves horizontally through two show scenes before it reaches the drop shaft. Once there, the cabin is pulled up and down faster than gravity in a randomized sequence, so the number, order and length of the drops vary between rides. At the top, doors open onto a view over the whole park for about a second and a half before the floor disappears.

It is the ride that separates people at this park. Some visitors ride it four times in a day. Some will not board it under any circumstances. There is no useful middle ground, and no amount of describing it makes it less intense.
experience: Walk the standby queue at least once. The Lightning Lane entrance skips the gardens and most of the lobby, which is a bad trade for a first-timer. The lobby is the single best room in the park and the pre-show film in the library is essential setup for the ride's tone.

The boiler room is long, dark and hot, then you board a bench of two rows facing forward with a seatbelt across your lap. The vehicle travels forward out of the shaft, through two effects scenes, then locks into the drop shaft. There is a pause here that is longer than you expect and it is the worst part for anyone nervous.

Sit in the back row and on an outside seat. The back row gets more air time on the drops, and the outside seats have the better view when the doors open at the top. The on-ride photo fires during the first big drop and is taken from in front of you, which is why everyone's face in that photo is honest.
tips: The drop profile is randomized between rides, so consecutive rides give you a genuinely different sequence. That is the argument for riding it twice.
Back row, outside seat, is the best combination: strongest airtime and the clearest view through the doors at the top.
Do the standby queue on your first ride even if you hold a Lightning Lane. The Lightning Lane route skips the gardens and most of the lobby.
Pockets empty out on the drops. Anything loose goes into a zipped pocket or the free cubbies at the load platform, and glasses need a strap.

Repeat visitors: the lobby set changes subtly over the years but the mail on the front desk, the luggage tags and the card room to the left of the queue reward a slow walk. Ask a bellhop about the hotel and they will stay in character for as long as you keep asking.
attractions.bestTime: Rope drop, or the last hour of the night when the crowd is at the nighttime show.
attractions.typicalWait: 35 to 70 minutes most of the day; under 25 in the first 30 minutes and the last 45.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Tower of Terror?
faqs.a: 40 inches. Note that clearing the stick and being ready for the ride are two very different things; a lot of children who measure 40 inches find this attraction genuinely traumatic. Rider switch is available.

faqs.q: How many drops does Tower of Terror have?
faqs.a: It varies. The drop sequence is randomized by the ride computer, so the number, height and rhythm of the drops differ between rides. That is deliberate and it is why the ride does not get less intense with repetition.

faqs.q: Is Tower of Terror scarier than Rock 'n' Roller Coaster?
faqs.a: For most people, yes, and by a wide margin. Rock 'n' Roller Coaster is a fast, loud, over-in-ninety-seconds launch coaster. Tower of Terror builds dread for ten minutes and then drops you repeatedly in the dark. People who dislike heights and falling should choose the coaster.

faqs.q: How tall is the drop?
faqs.a: The building stands 199 feet, and the drop shaft runs most of that height. The cabin is pulled downward faster than free-fall, which is why you lift off the seat rather than simply falling.

faqs.q: Can you get off if you change your mind?
faqs.a: Yes, up until you are seated and belted. Cast members will walk you out of the queue at any point, and there is a chicken exit before the boarding area. Once the vehicle leaves the load platform there is no way to stop it.

faqs.q: Does the queue itself have anything scary in it?
faqs.a: The queue is atmospheric rather than frightening, though the lobby is dim and the library pre-show has a sudden lightning effect and a burst of static that startles small children. Nothing jumps out at you.

attractions.name: Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring The Muppets

scary.notes: It is pitch dark, it launches from a standstill to highway speed in under three seconds, and it turns you upside down three times. Nothing in it is designed to frighten you, but the combination of darkness, speed and inversions is a lot for a first-time coaster rider. The 48-inch requirement is the tallest at Hollywood Studios and it screens out most of the children who would struggle.

accessibility.notes: You must transfer into a coaster seat with an over-the-shoulder harness; the step over the side of the car is high and the harness does not accommodate every body shape, so there is a test seat outside the entrance. Guests with back, neck or heart conditions, and anyone who has had recent surgery, should not ride.

attractions.summary: A pitch-dark indoor launch coaster with three inversions that goes from a standstill to highway speed in under three seconds; 48 inches to ride.
description: This is the fastest and most aggressive ride at Hollywood Studios. A twenty-four passenger train sits at a dead stop, a countdown runs, and then a linear induction launch throws you from zero to roughly sixty miles an hour in under three seconds, straight into a rollover loop. What follows is about ninety seconds of indoor track in near-total darkness with three inversions, all set to a soundtrack piped through speakers in your headrest.

The coaster opened in 1999 and ran for twenty-six years with an Aerosmith theme. It was rethemed to the Muppets and reopened to all guests on May 26, 2026, at the same 48-inch height requirement and with no virtual queue. The track layout, the launch and the inversions are unchanged; the story, the pre-show, the queue decor and the soundtrack are new.

The Muppets framing works better than it has any right to. The premise is that you are late to a show and being driven there at an unreasonable speed by characters with no regard for traffic law, which is a more sensible reason for a stretch limousine to invert three times than the previous version ever had. It also gives the ride a comic tone that takes some of the edge off the queue without softening the ride itself.
experience: The queue is indoors and air conditioned after the first switchback, which makes it far more tolerable than the Slinky Dog Dash line on a hot afternoon. The pre-show puts you in a room where the situation is explained by characters on screens, then you walk out to the launch track.

Board and pull the harness down firmly. The launch is the moment: a countdown, a real physical push into the seat back, and the first inversion arrives about two seconds later before your brain has caught up. From there it is a run of turns and two more inversions with essentially no let-up until the brakes.

Sit in the front row if you want to see the lighting and the effects, which are much easier to read from there. Sit in the back row if you want the strongest launch; the back car is whipped through the launch section and hits the first inversion at a noticeably higher perceived speed. The on-ride photo is captured during the launch.
tips: Back row for the strongest launch, front row for the best look at the lighting effects. The queue splits for row selection near the load platform.
48 inches is the tallest height requirement at Hollywood Studios, and there is no way around it. Rider switch is available and is the correct plan for a family with one child under the line.
There is a test seat outside the entrance. Use it before queueing if the over-the-shoulder harness might be a problem; the restraint is less forgiving than most modern coasters.
Empty your pockets completely. The three inversions will take a phone out of a loose pocket and there is no net over the track.
Repeat visitors: the ride audio is per-train rather than per-park, so different trains run different soundtrack mixes. Riding twice in a row usually gets you a different track.
attractions.bestTime: First 30 minutes of the day, or during the nighttime show when Sunset Boulevard crowds shift to the amphitheater.
attractions.typicalWait: 40 to 80 minutes through the day; under 30 at rope drop and in the final hour.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring The Muppets?
faqs.a: 48 inches, the tallest requirement at Hollywood Studios. It is measured with shoes on at the entrance and enforced strictly. Rider switch is offered for parties with a child below the line.

faqs.q: Does Rock 'n' Roller Coaster go upside down?
faqs.a: Yes, three times: two rollover loops and a corkscrew. It is the only inverting coaster at Walt Disney World, and the whole layout runs in the dark, so you often cannot tell which inversion you are in.

faqs.q: Is this still the Aerosmith version?
faqs.a: No. The coaster was rethemed to the Muppets and reopened to all guests on May 26, 2026. The track, launch and inversions are identical; the queue, pre-show, story and soundtrack are new.

faqs.q: How fast does it go?
faqs.a: The launch takes the train from a standstill to roughly sixty miles an hour in under three seconds, which is the fastest acceleration of any ride at Walt Disney World. Top speed after that is not the point; the launch is.

faqs.q: Is it scarier than Tower of Terror?
faqs.a: For most people, no. It is more physically intense but far shorter and it does not build dread the way Tower of Terror does. People who hate falling generally prefer this; people who hate speed and inversions prefer the tower.

faqs.q: Is there a single rider line?
faqs.a: No single rider queue is offered at this attraction. Rider switch is available, and it is the practical option for families splitting around the height requirement.

attractions.name: Beauty and the Beast: Live on Stage

scary.notes: A daytime musical with a villain, a fight and a brief storm sequence near the end that involves loud effects and dramatic lighting. Toddlers occasionally find the Beast's first appearance and the confrontation scene startling. Nothing else in it troubles anyone.

accessibility.notes: Accessible seating is on the flat rows at the rear and along the side aisles of the Theater of the Stars, reached without steps. The benches have no backs. Sign language interpretation runs on a published schedule rather than every performance.

attractions.summary: A 25-minute condensed stage musical of the 1991 film in a covered amphitheater on Sunset Boulevard, running since the park's early years.
description: This is a genuine Broadway-style production compressed to twenty-five minutes: live singers, a full costume department, choreographed ensemble numbers and a set that transforms twice. It has run at this park in some form since 1991, which makes it one of the longest-running stage shows at any Disney park, and the production values have been maintained rather than allowed to slide.
The show does the obvious hits from the film and cuts everything else. That is the right call. It gets in, delivers three big numbers, resolves, and gets out before anyone under eight loses interest.

The Theater of the Stars is covered but open-sided, which means shade without air conditioning. That is a meaningful improvement over standing in the sun, but it is not a cool room, and a 2pm performance in August is still a hot twenty-five minutes.
experience: The amphitheater seats around fifteen hundred on backless benches. Arriving twenty minutes early gets you a choice of seat; ten minutes gets you a seat. It very rarely fills to capacity, which is why using a Lightning Lane Multi Pass here is close to wasted.

The show runs three main sequences: the opening ensemble number in the village, the ballroom set piece which is the visual high point, and the confrontation and resolution. The costume work on the enchanted household characters is the detail worth watching for; the puppetry and articulation are better than the show's reputation.

Sit in the center block toward the back for the best overall view of the choreography, or in the front third if you have a small child who wants to see faces. The far side blocks have a compromised view of the upper level of the set.
tips: Sit toward the back of the center block. The choreography is built for a wide view and the front rows lose the shape of the ensemble numbers.
The theater is covered but not air conditioned. It is shade rather than relief, so bring water for an afternoon performance.
Never spend a Lightning Lane Multi Pass on this. The amphitheater holds fifteen hundred and almost never fills.
The last performance of the day is usually the least crowded and the coolest, and it puts you on Sunset Boulevard right where you want to be for the nighttime show.

Repeat visitors: the production has been restaged more than once since 1991, with revised costumes and a reworked ballroom sequence, so it is not the show you saw as a child even though the running order is familiar.
attractions.bestTime: The last performance of the day: cooler, emptier, and it leaves you positioned for the nighttime show.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue. Arrive 10 to 20 minutes early for a good seat.

faqs.q: How long is Beauty and the Beast: Live on Stage?
faqs.a: About 25 minutes. Add 10 to 20 minutes of seating beforehand if you want a choice of where you sit, and note that the benches have no backs.

faqs.q: Is the show air conditioned?
faqs.a: No. The Theater of the Stars has a roof but open sides, so you get shade and whatever breeze is moving. On a hot afternoon it is better than standing in the sun but it is not a cooling break.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for toddlers?
faqs.a: Yes, with one caveat. The Beast's first appearance and the confrontation near the end use loud effects and dramatic lighting, and a few small children find those moments startling. There is no height or age requirement of any kind.

faqs.q: Do you need a Lightning Lane for it?
faqs.a: No. The amphitheater seats around fifteen hundred people and rarely fills. Walking up ten to twenty minutes before showtime is enough on almost any day.

faqs.q: Is it the same show as the Broadway version?
faqs.a: No. This is a condensed 25-minute adaptation built around the film's main musical numbers, with original staging for this theater. The full-length stage musical is a separate production and is not performed here.

attractions.name: Fantasmic!

scary.notes: The villain sequence is the whole issue. A long stretch of the show is given over to Disney villains, with fire on the water, a very large dragon effect and heavy low-end sound. It is genuinely too much for a lot of children under five, particularly at the end of a long day when they are already fried. Everything before and after it is gentle.

accessibility.notes: The Hollywood Hills Amphitheater has designated accessible sections reached without stairs, but the general seating is steep stadium benches with a long climb, and the walk in from Sunset Boulevard is uphill. Ask a cast member at the entrance to be routed to accessible seating rather than trying to find it yourself in the crowd.

attractions.summary: The park's nighttime show: a 30-minute water, fire and projection spectacular in a 6,900-seat amphitheater, with live performers and boats.
description: Fantasmic! is staged in a purpose-built amphitheater carved into the hillside behind Sunset Boulevard, using a lagoon, an island stage, three walls of water used as projection screens, fire effects, live performers, a floating barge and a very large dragon. It opened at this park in October 1998 and it remains the biggest single production Walt Disney World stages on a nightly basis.

The framing is that you are inside Mickey Mouse's dream, which drifts through a run of musical sequences, turns into a nightmare when the villains take over, and resolves. That structure is thirty years old and it shows in places, but the practical effects are the reason to go: water screens and real fire simply read differently in person than projections on a building do.

The cost is your evening. The amphitheater seats about 6,900 and on a busy night it fills, which means claiming a seat well before showtime and then sitting in it. Weigh that honestly. Two more rides at low nighttime waits is a real alternative use of that hour.
experience: The queue forms on Sunset Boulevard and the amphitheater opens roughly seventy-five minutes before showtime on busy nights, less on quiet ones. Once the gates open the walk in is uphill and the benches are steep concrete stadium seating with no backs.

Sit in the center sections, about halfway up. Low seats put the water screens above your sightline and get you misted; the highest rows lose the depth of the fire effects. The far left and right sections have a badly angled view of the water screens and are the sections cast members fill last for a reason.

The show runs about thirty minutes. The first third is gentle, the middle is the villain sequence with the fire and the dragon, and the last third is the resolution and the boat parade. Leaving early to beat the crowd costs you the best two minutes and saves about ten; walking out during the finale is a bad trade.
tips: Center section, halfway up. That is the sweet spot for the water screens and the fire, and it keeps you out of the mist zone in the first several rows.
The front rows get genuinely damp from the water screens. On a cool night that matters more than people expect.

A Lightning Lane Multi Pass selection here gets you into a reserved seating area but not a better seat than arriving forty minutes early does. It is worth it only if you would rather ride during that window.
The villain sequence is the part that upsets small children, and it lasts several minutes. If your child is already tired, watch the projection show on Hollywood Boulevard instead.

Repeat visitors: the amphitheater empties from the top down, so seats in the upper center let you leave first even though they feel further from the exit. The lower sections take fifteen minutes to clear.
attractions.bestTime: The second performance on nights when two are scheduled; it plays to roughly half the crowd of the first.
attractions.typicalWait: Arrive 45 to 75 minutes before showtime on a busy night; 25 to 30 minutes is enough on a quiet one.

faqs.q: How early should you arrive for Fantasmic?
faqs.a: On a busy night, 45 to 75 minutes before showtime for a good center seat. On a quiet night or for a second performance, 25 to 30 minutes is usually enough. The amphitheater holds about 6,900 people, so it does fill on peak dates.

faqs.q: Is Fantasmic scary for young children?
faqs.a: The villain sequence is, and it runs for several minutes with fire on the water, heavy sound and a very large dragon effect. Children under five who are already tired often find it too much. The rest of the show is gentle.

faqs.q: Where are the best seats for Fantasmic?
faqs.a: Center sections, roughly halfway up. The water screens sit above the sightline from the lowest rows and the fire effects lose depth from the very top. The far left and right sections have a poor angle on the projections.

faqs.q: Do you get wet at Fantasmic?
faqs.a: Only in the first several rows, and only lightly, from spray off the water screens. Nobody needs a poncho, but if you are sitting front and center on a cool evening you will notice it.

faqs.q: Is a Lightning Lane Multi Pass worth it for Fantasmic?
faqs.a: Only if you want to use the pre-show hour riding instead of sitting. The reserved area is not a better view than a seat you claim forty minutes early, so the value is entirely in the time it frees up.

faqs.q: Does Fantasmic run every night?
faqs.a: Not always, and on some nights it runs twice. The schedule varies with the season and the park's operating hours, so check the entertainment tab in the app on the day rather than assuming.

attractions.name: Lightning McQueen's Racing Academy

scary.notes: A standing theater show with a large screen and one moment where things go wrong loudly. Nothing chases anyone and nothing is dark for long. Very young children occasionally jump at the crash sound effect.

accessibility.notes: Step-free standing theater with designated spaces for wheelchairs and ECVs at the rear, which have a clear view because the room is flat and the screen is high. There is no seating, so a ten-minute stand is required unless you bring your own.

attractions.summary: A ten-minute standing show in the Sunset Showcase where a full-size Lightning McQueen vehicle appears on a wraparound screen stage.
description: The Sunset Showcase theater holds a wide wraparound screen and a physical Lightning McQueen vehicle on a rig in front of it. The show has him deliver a racing lesson that goes wrong, with the screen simulating a track, and it lasts about ten minutes standing.

It is aimed squarely at children under about eight who like the Cars films, and for them it lands well. For anyone else it is ten minutes of air conditioning in a part of the park that badly needs more of it, which is a reasonable enough reason to walk in.

The queue is short and the theater turns over quickly, so this is one of the lowest-commitment things at Hollywood Studios. It is also right next door to two of the park's two longest coaster queues, which makes it a useful place to stash half your party.
tips: It is standing room only for about ten minutes. Bring a stroller-free plan or be ready to hold a small child.
Stand toward the back and center. The screen wraps, and from the front you cannot take in the whole image.
There are character photo ops in the exit area that most people walk straight past.
Repeat visitors: the Sunset Showcase is a flexible venue that Disney uses for other programming at times, so confirm in the app that this show is running on the day you visit.
attractions.bestTime: Midday, as an air-conditioned break between Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster.
attractions.typicalWait: 5 to 20 minutes, driven by where the current showing is in its cycle.

attractions.name: Walt Disney Presents

scary.notes: A self-paced museum corridor and a small theater. There is nothing here that frightens anyone. The only warning worth giving is that a child under eight will be bored within four minutes.

accessibility.notes: Entirely step-free with wide corridors and a level theater at the end with removable seating for wheelchairs. Display cases are at a height readable from a seated position. The film at the end runs with captions available on request.

attractions.summary: A self-paced museum of Walt Disney's career with original artifacts, park models and a short film, and the quietest room in the park.
description: This is a walk-through exhibition covering Walt Disney's life and the company's history, running from early animation through the theme parks. It contains genuinely significant objects: original artwork, awards, a scale model of a Disneyland attraction, letters, and the desk-and-office material that most Disney fans have only seen photographed.

It ends in a small theater showing a documentary short. You can walk the corridor in fifteen minutes or take forty-five if you read the cases, and nobody rushes you. There is no queue, ever, which given the rest of this park's wait times is remarkable.

The other half of the building is used to preview upcoming films and projects. That portion changes, so treat it as a bonus rather than a reason to visit. The permanent exhibition is the reason, and it is the best free thirty minutes at Hollywood Studios for anyone over about twelve.
experience: You enter into a corridor of display cases arranged roughly chronologically. The early sections cover the animation studio's founding and the shift to feature films; the middle covers the parks, including a large model and original concept work; the last stretch covers the company after Walt's death.

The theater at the end runs a documentary on a loop, about fifteen minutes long, in a cool room with proper seating. On a hot afternoon that theater is one of the best places in the park to sit down. Nobody polices how many times you watch it.

The single best object is different for everyone, but the park model and the original attraction artwork consistently stop people who came in expecting a hallway of posters. Look at the small labels; several of the items are one-of-a-kind.
tips: There is never a wait. This is the reliable fallback when a ride goes down and you need somewhere to be for thirty minutes.
The theater at the end is air conditioned with real seats and runs continuously, which makes it the best free sit-down in the park.
The preview area near the front changes and is not the point. Walk past it if the current preview does not interest you; the permanent exhibition is behind it.
Do not bring a child under eight expecting them to engage. Pair this with the Disney Junior show next door and split the party.
Repeat visitors: the display cases are rotated periodically as items go out on loan or into conservation, so a case you remember may hold something different now.
attractions.bestTime: Any time; it is never busy. Best used in the afternoon heat or when a headliner goes down.
attractions.typicalWait: No wait at any point in the day.

faqs.q: How long does Walt Disney Presents take?
faqs.a: Fifteen minutes if you walk it, forty-five if you read everything, plus about fifteen more for the film at the end. It is entirely self-paced and there is no queue at any point.

faqs.q: Is Walt Disney Presents worth doing?
faqs.a: For adults with any interest in Disney history, it is one of the best-value stops in the park and it costs you no waiting at all. For young children it is a corridor of glass cases and they will be done in four minutes.

faqs.q: Is there air conditioning?
faqs.a: Yes, throughout, including a proper theater with seating at the end. It is one of the most reliable places in this park to cool off without buying anything or queueing.

faqs.q: Are the items on display real?
faqs.a: Many are original artifacts, including artwork, awards and park models, with a few reproductions clearly labeled as such. Items rotate over time as pieces go out for conservation or loan.

faqs.q: Do you need a Lightning Lane?
faqs.a: No. There is no queue and no Lightning Lane for this attraction. You walk in whenever you like.

attractions.name: Disney Junior Play and Dance!

scary.notes: A bright, loud, participatory dance party aimed at preschoolers. There is nothing frightening in it. The volume and the crowd of excited children can overwhelm a sensory-sensitive child, which is the only real caution.

accessibility.notes: Step-free with a flat open floor and no fixed seating, so wheelchairs and ECVs can position anywhere including near the front. Most of the audience sits on the floor, which means a seated guest has a clear sightline. There is no dimming and no strobe.

attractions.summary: A 20-minute interactive dance party for preschoolers with Disney Junior characters, in an air-conditioned theater with an open floor.
description: This is a live show built for children roughly two to seven: a host leads dancing and games, Disney Junior characters appear, bubbles and streamers come out, and the whole room is encouraged to move. There is no seating in the traditional sense; families sit or stand on an open floor and children go to the front.

It is one of only a handful of things at Hollywood Studios designed for children too small for the height requirements, which is why it matters more here than the equivalent show would at Magic Kingdom. This park has seven attractions with height sticks and very little else for a four-year-old.
For accompanying adults, it is twenty minutes of air conditioning and a place to sit on a floor. That is not nothing on day three of a trip.
experience: The theater fills between shows and empties completely, so the practical approach is to arrive about ten minutes before a scheduled start. Children are encouraged forward and parents hang back, which works better than it sounds because the room is flat and open.

The show runs through a set of songs and games with two or three character appearances. The characters do not do individual greetings, so this is not a substitute for a meet, though children get close enough for a decent photo from the floor.

The finale involves streamers or bubbles over the front of the room. If your child wants to be in the middle of that, get them to the front early; if you would rather not pick confetti out of a stroller, stay back.
tips: Send children forward and stand at the back. The room is designed for that split and the sightlines work from anywhere.
It is genuinely one of the few Hollywood Studios attractions for a child under 32 inches, which makes it a scheduling anchor rather than a filler.
The character lineup rotates and is not published far in advance, so check the app the morning of if a specific character matters.
There is no seating. If standing for twenty minutes is a problem, sit on the floor with everyone else or use a wheelchair space at the side.
Repeat visitors: this show has been restaged more than once under different names in the same theater, so the format you remember from a previous trip may not be the current one.
attractions.bestTime: Mid-morning or mid-afternoon, when you need air conditioning and the ride queues are long.
attractions.typicalWait: No queue between shows; arrive about 10 minutes before a scheduled start.

faqs.q: What age is Disney Junior Play and Dance for?
faqs.a: Roughly two to seven. Children older than about eight tend to find it too young, and children under two mostly enjoy the noise and the bubbles without following the games.

faqs.q: Is there seating?
faqs.a: No traditional seating. The theater has an open flat floor where families sit or stand, with children encouraged toward the front. Wheelchair and ECV spaces are available at the sides and rear.

faqs.q: Do you get to meet the characters?
faqs.a: No. Characters appear on stage during the show but there are no individual greetings, photos or autographs. It is a performance, not a meet and greet.

faqs.q: Is it worth a Lightning Lane Multi Pass?
faqs.a: No. The theater empties completely between performances and arriving ten minutes early is enough on almost any day. Save the selection for a ride.

faqs.q: How long is the show?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes, running several times a day. Times are posted in the entertainment section of the app on the day of your visit.

attractions.name: Star Wars Launch Bay

scary.notes: A dim exhibition hall with props and character greetings. The dark-side character greeting is staged to be intimidating and a few small children back out of it. Nothing else in the building troubles anyone.

accessibility.notes: Step-free throughout with wide corridors and level greeting rooms. Lighting is deliberately low and some display labels are hard to read; a phone torch is fine to use. Character greeting rooms have room to turn a wheelchair.

attractions.summary: An indoor Star Wars exhibition hall with film props, replicas and queued character greetings, and almost always the shortest line in the park.
description: Launch Bay opened in 2015 in the old animation building and it has been quietly useful ever since. It is a large, cool, dim hall containing film props and replicas, a screening room, and separate rooms where you queue to meet Star Wars characters with a PhotoPass photographer.

Galaxy's Edge overshadowed it completely, which is precisely why it is worth knowing about. The character greetings here are the reliable, queued alternative to the roaming encounters in Galaxy's Edge: you know who you are meeting, you know you will get a photo, and the wait is usually under twenty minutes.
It is also a large air-conditioned room in a part of the park where those are scarce, and nobody is in a hurry to move you along.
tips: This is where you go if a child specifically wants a guaranteed photo with a named Star Wars character. Galaxy's Edge encounters are better but entirely unpredictable.
The character lineup rotates. Check the app the morning of if a particular character is the point of the visit.
The prop hall is genuinely worth ten minutes on its own, and it is empty most of the day while every ride queue nearby runs over an hour.
Repeat visitors: the exhibition contents have been revised several times since 2015 as new films arrived, so the props you saw on a previous trip are unlikely to all still be there.
attractions.bestTime: Afternoon, when you need a cool indoor room and the character queues elsewhere are at their longest.
attractions.typicalWait: 10 to 25 minutes for character greetings; no wait for the exhibition hall itself.

attractions.name: Voyage of the Little Mermaid
attractions.closedNote: Stopped performing in March 2020 and never reopened. The theater in Animation Courtyard has since been used for other programming.

scary.notes: The theater was very dark and the sea witch appeared as a large puppet with thunder and lighting effects, which frightened a meaningful number of small children. Historical entry only; the show no longer performs.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The show is not performing.

attractions.summary: The puppet-and-live-performer stage show that ran from 1992 to 2020; the theater still stands but the show has not returned.
description: A seventeen-minute condensed staging of the film using black-light puppetry, live performers, laser effects and a water curtain, in a dark theater built to feel like being underwater. The sea witch was staged as an enormous puppet that filled the proscenium and was the moment everyone remembered, for better or worse.
It stopped performing in March 2020 and never came back. The theater still stands in Animation Courtyard and has been used for other purposes since.
It is one of the most-searched closed attractions at this park because it ran for twenty-eight years and a generation of visitors remembers it. There is no announced plan to bring it back.
tips: The show has not performed since 2020 and no return has been announced.
Beauty and the Beast: Live on Stage on Sunset Boulevard is the surviving condensed-musical show at this park and is the closest equivalent.
The Animation Courtyard theater building is still there, so an operating-looking facade does not mean the show is running.
Repeat visitors: the black-light puppetry technique used here is no longer used in any operating show at Walt Disney World.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the show is not currently performing.

attractions.name: The Magic of Disney Animation
attractions.closedNote: Closed July 12, 2015. The building was repurposed and now houses Star Wars Launch Bay.

scary.notes: A tour of a working animation studio with a film and a drawing class. Nothing in it frightened anyone. Historical entry only.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The attraction is not operating and the building now houses Star Wars Launch Bay.

attractions.summary: The tour of the park's working animation studio, with a drawing class at the end; closed in 2015 and now the Star Wars Launch Bay building.
description: For its first decade this was a tour of a genuine, functioning Disney animation studio with artists working behind glass on films that were actually in production. Several features were animated in part in this building. After the Florida studio closed in 2004 the attraction continued in a reduced form, with a film, character greetings and an animation class where a Disney artist taught guests to draw a character step by step.
It closed in July 2015 and the building became Star Wars Launch Bay. The drawing class was the part people miss most, and nothing at Walt Disney World currently replaces it.
The loss of this attraction, along with the Backlot Tour, is the clearest marker of this park's shift away from being about how films get made.
tips: The attraction closed in 2015. The building is now Star Wars Launch Bay, which you can still walk into.
Walt Disney Presents next door is the surviving attraction about how Disney animation actually worked, and it is worth thirty minutes.
There is no animation drawing class at any Walt Disney World park today.
Repeat visitors: the exterior architecture of Animation Courtyard is largely unchanged, so the building you remember is the one Launch Bay occupies.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.

attractions.name: The Legend of Captain Jack Sparrow
attractions.closedNote: Closed in 2018. The space in the Animation Courtyard building was absorbed into other uses.

scary.notes: A dark standing walkthrough with projected undead pirates, sudden loud effects and a fog-and-water finale. It startled small children reliably. Historical entry only.

accessibility.notes: Historical entry. The attraction is not operating.

attractions.summary: A short walkthrough show with projected pirates and practical effects that ran in Animation Courtyard from 2012 to 2018.
description: Guests stood in a dark room while a projected Captain Jack Sparrow ran them through a compressed pirate adventure, with fog, water, wind and projection effects delivering the set pieces. It was ten minutes long, it was free of any queue most of the day, and it filled a gap in a corner of the park that had little else.
It closed in 2018 and the space was absorbed into other uses in the Animation Courtyard building.
It is listed here for completeness. It was never a headliner, but people who visited between 2012 and 2018 remember it and search for it by name.
tips: The attraction closed in 2018 and there is nothing to see at the site.
For Pirates of the Caribbean content at Walt Disney World, the ride at Magic Kingdom is the only current option.
Star Wars Launch Bay in the same building is the current walkthrough in Animation Courtyard and is worth a stop.
Repeat visitors: the entrance that led to this show is no longer marked, so do not go looking for it in the courtyard.
attractions.bestTime: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
attractions.typicalWait: Not applicable; the attraction is permanently closed.
